records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	the total number of proposals received and sanctioned under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) from Uttar Pradesh during the last three years; <br/><br/>(b)	whether all sanctioned work under the scheme has been commenced and completed within the promised deadlines, if not, the reasons for delay in starting the work, 	project-wise; <br/><br/>(c)	the details of proposals made and work currently underway in the District of Unnao in Uttar Pradesh along with the details of work sanctioned and completed during the last 	year within the district; and <br/><br/>(d)	the measures taken to assess and maintain the quality of work under the scheme?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI RAM KRIPAL YADAV)<br/><br/>(a)& (b):	The total number of proposals received and sanctioned under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) in the State of Uttar Pradesh during the last three years is given below:-<br/><br/>Year	 Proposal received   Proposal         Value of<br/>         (No. of works)	    sanctioned        sanctioned                    <br/>                           (No. of works)     proposal  <br/>                                             (Rs. in crore)<br/><br/>2015-16	      NIL	        NIL	        NIL<br/><br/>2016-17	      681	        681	      3140.90<br/><br/>2017-18	       35	         35	       268.82<br/><br/>Out of 716 works sanctioned in the years 2016-17 and 2017-18, 15 works were subsequently de-sanctioned. <br/><br/>All the remaining 701 sanctioned works has started and 633 completed. Work on 68 road works is under progress. The status of these road works is given in Annexure. <br/><br/>(c):	No road work under PMGSY was sanctioned in the District of Unnao during the years 2015-16 and 2017-18. 9 road works were sanctioned in the District during the year 2016-17, which have already been completed. No work under PMGSY is currently underway in the District. <br/><br/>(d):	PMGSY has a well structured three-tier Quality Control mechanism for ensuring construction of quality road works and durability of road assets under PMGSY.  Under the first tier, the Programme Implementation Units (PIUs) are required to ensure process control through mandatory tests on material and workmanship at field laboratory.  The second tier is a structured independent quality monitoring at the State level through State Quality Monitors (SQMs) to ensure that every work is inspected at initial stage, middle stage and final stage of the construction.  Under the third tier, independent National Quality Monitors (NQMs) are deployed for random inspection of road works to monitor quality and also to provide guidance of senior professionals to the field functionaries. Based on the periodic monitoring of quality of roads under the 3-tier mechanism, corrective measures, wherever necessary, are taken by the State Governments.<br/><br/>*****<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) the present status of progress made to provide e-Panchayat facility in all the Panchayats in Uttar Pradesh;<br/>(b) the number of Panchayats which have been provided with internet/e-Panchayat facility and the number of Panchayats yet to get this facility, in Uttar Pradesh; and<br/>(c) the time by which all the Panchayats in the country are likely to be equipped with the said facility?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ<br/>(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA)<br/><br/>(a)	Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) has been implementing e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) that seeks to transform the functioning of all the Panchayats, making them more transparent, accountable and effective as organs of decentralized self-governing institutions. Under e-Panchayat MMP, Panchayat Enterprise Suite (PES) - a suite of core software applications has been developed to address various aspects of Panchayats’ functioning including planning, budgeting, implementation, accounting, monitoring, social audit and delivery of citizen services like issue of certificates, licenses, tax collection etc.<br/>	Panchayat being a State subject, adoption of these applications and providing e-Panchayat facility at the Gram Panchayat level are primarily the responsibility of concerned State Government/ Union Territory (UT) administration. The State Government of Uttar Pradesh has informed that under e-Panchayat, PES applications namely, Local Government Directory, PlanPlus, ActionaSoft, PRIASoft etc. have been implemented in all the Gram Panchayats (GPs) of the State. Besides, 8000 Gram Panchayat Secretaries have been equipped with laptops and internet dongles.<br/><br/>(b)	For attaining the vision of Digital India, BharatNet project is being implemented by Department of Telecommunications in a phased manner to create network to connect all the GPs by broadband in the country. As part of BharatNet project, the Last Mile connectivity is being provided through Wi-Fi or any other suitable broadband technology to access broadband /internet services to all the GPs in the country.<br/>	The Department of Telecommunications has informed that in Uttar Pradesh, as on 03.02.2019, out of total 55,095 GPs (approximately) in the State, 28065 GPs have been made Service Ready. Further, Wi-Fi hotspots have been installed at 25,211 GPs and out of them, services are being provided in 2,461 GPs.<br/><br/>(c)	The Department of Telecommunications has informed that the BharatNet project is targeted to be completed by March, 2019.<br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Delay in operationalisation of Lucknow Delhi Tejas Express
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	the reasons for non-operationalisation of the Lucknow-Delhi Tejas Express promised by Government in the Railway budget of 2016-17 till date;<br/><br/>(b)	 the anticipated date by which the train would begin operations; and<br/><br/>(c)	the details of the fare of the Tejas Express, as decided by the Railways?<br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI RAJEN GOHAIN)<br/><br/>(a)	& (b): During the Railway Budget 2016-17, the then Hon’ble Minister of Railways announced the introduction of four new type of train services which interalia included Tejas Express. Subsequent to this announcement, it was decided to introduce 12585/12586 Lucknow Jn.-New Delhi Tejas Express. The operationalisation of 12585/12586 Lucknow Jn.-New Delhi Tejas Express was pending due to non-availability of rake. As of now, the train is ready for introduction and earnest efforts are being made to introduce the train at the earliest.<br/><br/>(c): The Basic fare of AC Chair car and Executive class of Tejas Express is 1.20 times of the basic fare of respective classes of Shatabdi Express trains.<br/><br/>******<br/><br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	 whether it is a fact that agrarian unrest has been growing with violent consequences in the last one- year;<br/><br/>(b)	 whether Government has not  fulfilled its promise of providing at least 1.5 times the production cost while procuring produce from farmers;<br/><br/>(c)	 if so, the measures taken by Government to sensitise farmers to shift to mixed farming practices based on scientific inputs; and<br/><br/>(d)	 the schemes implemented by Government to prevent losses in the event of bumper production?	<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE <br/><br/>(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA)<br/><br/>(a):   From time to time, the farmers and their various organizations have expressed their views on various agrarian issues and submitted memorandum/representation to Government.<br/><br/>(b) & (c):    No Sir.  The Government has been increasing the  Minimum Support Price (MSP) for various agricultural commodities to incentivize farmers to bring more area under cultivation of crops and to invest on increasing the productivity. Giving a major boost for the farmers’ income, the Government has increased the Minimum Support Prices  (MSPs) of all Kharif & Rabi crops for 2018-19 Season. This decision of the Government is a historic one as it redeems the promise of the pre-determined principle of fixing the MSPs at a level of at least 150 percent of the cost of production announced by the Union Budget for 2018-19.<br/><br/>(d):     Agriculture being a State subject, the State Governments undertakes development of perspective plans and ensures effective implementation of the programmes/ schemes. Also, Government of India supplements the efforts of the State Governments through various Schemes/ Programmes. The income approach focuses on achieving high productivity, reduced cost of cultivation and remunerative price on the produce, with a view to earn higher profits from farming  including adoption of farming produces based on scientific inputs.<br/><br/>The Government is implementing National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) scheme for transparent price discovery for remunerative prices for the farmers for their produce through competitive online bidding system. So far, 585 wholesale regulated markets of 16 States and 02 UTs have   been   integrated with   e-NAM   platform.     Under  the scheme, apart from providing technical <br/>Contd….2/-<br/><br/><br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/>  support, financial assistance upto Rs. 75 lakh per mandi for electronic weighing scale, computer IT equipments, assaying equipments, cleaning/ sorting/ grading equipments and bio- composting unit is also provided to States/Union Territories (UTs).  Government of India in association with concerned state government is also promoting FPOs to enable them to reach economy of scale and better access to markets for better realization of prices.<br/><br/> In addition, Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), a Centrally Sponsored Scheme is being implemented for holistic growth of the horticulture sector covering fruits (including Mango), vegetables, root and tuber crops, mushrooms, spices, flowers, aromatic plants, coconut, cashew, cocoa and bamboo.  Assistance is extended for establishment of infrastructure relating to cold chain management viz. Pre-cooling units, on farm pack houses, mobile pre-cooling units, staging cold rooms, cold storage units, integrated cold chain supply system, refrigerated vans/ containers, primary/ mobile processing units, ripening chambers, evaporative/ low energy cool chambers, preservation units etc. under Integrated Post Harvest management component of MIDH. 	<br/>*******<br/><br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that Government has not yet taken any action against more than a dozen universities of the country that have been found to be fake;<br/>(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and<br/>(c) if not, the action taken against those universities and the new rules put in place to ensure such fake universities do not open in future?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/><br/>(DR. SATYA PAL SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): The Central Government as well as the University Grants Commission (UGC) has taken the following action against fake Universities running without recognition:<br/>i.	UGC has issued Show Cause / Warning Notices to fake Universities cautioned that running of Undergraduate and Postgraduate degree courses and giving misleading advertisements shall attract severe action under the provisions of appropriate laws including the UGC Act and the Indian Penal Code, etc.<br/>ii.	Letters have been sent to the State/UT Principal Secretaries/Education Secretaries for taking appropriate action against the fake Universities located in their jurisdiction. <br/>iii.	UGC has lodged FIRs in the respective Police stations against Indian Institute of Planning and Management (IIPM), New Delhi and Bio-Chemic Education Grant Commission, Nadia, West Bengal.<br/>	Apart from the above, UGC has taken the following steps to spread awareness among the general public, students & parents from the fake Universities:<br/>i.	UGC has published the list of fake Universities on its website i.e. www.ugc.ac.in.<br/>ii.	UGC has also issued public notice against the unrecognized status of Indian Institute of Planning and Management (IIPM), New Delhi and illegal status of Bio-Chemic Education Grant Commission, Nadia, West Bengal.<br/>iii.	At the beginning of every academic session, UGC issues Press Release and Public Notice regarding State-wise list of fake Universities in the country in national dailies and newspapers in Hindi and English to warn the aspiring students, guardians and the public at large not to take admission in the courses run by the self-styled, unauthorized fake Universities/Institutions of higher education functioning in different parts of the country.  <br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: New phase of FAME India scheme
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has made available enough roadside charging stations in big cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Lucknow, Bengaluru, etc. to make the FAME India initiative  efficacious and if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government is considering to launch a new phase of the FAME India scheme and if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) the data on most successful vehicles in the two and four-wheleer segments respectively and their respective monetary incentives?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES & PUBLIC ENTERPRISES<br/>(SHRI BABUL SUPRIYO)<br/>---------- <br/><br/>(a) to (c): In order to promote manufacturing of electric and hybrid vehicle technology and to ensure sustainable growth of the same, Department of Heavy Industry formulated FAME India Scheme [Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India]. At present, the Phase-1 of FAME India Scheme is under implementation through four focus areas namely Demand Creation, Technology Platform, Pilot Project and Charging Infrastructure. The Phase-1 of FAME India Scheme was originally approved for a period of 2 years commencing from 1st April 2015, which has been extended from time to time thereafter and the last extension is allowed upto 31st March 2019. <br/><br/>The Phase-II of FAME India scheme proposes to give a push to electric vehicles (EVs) in public transport and seeks to encourage adoption of EVs by way of market creation and demand aggregation. The draft scheme has envisaged the holistic growth of EV industry, including providing for charging infrastructure, research & development of EV technologies and push towards greater indigenization. The scheme has not been finalized yet. <br/><br/>Under Charging Infrastructure focus area of FAME India Scheme (Phase-1), the Government has sanctioned following projects/proposals for establishment of charging infrastructures / stations –<br/><br/>S.No.	Name of the Project/Proposal	Implementing Agency / Organisation<br/>1  Public Fast Charging Infrastructure               M/s Mahindra Reva Electric Vehicles Pvt. Ltd.<br/>Network for Electric Vehicles at Bangalore    in collaboration with Lithium Urban               Technologies Pvt. Ltd.<br/>(Establishment of 25 DC Fast Charging Stations)<br/>	<br/>2  Proposal for putting up of Solar Based            Rajasthan Electronics & Instruments<br/>Charging Infrastructure for EVs                           Limited (REIL), Jaipur <br/>3  Proposal for putting up of Solar Based            Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited<br/>Charging Infrastructure for EVs                          (BHEL)<br/><br/>4  Proposal of Setting-up 200 Charging              Rajasthan Electronics & Instruments Limited<br/>Stations at Delhi, Jaipur & Chandigarh             (REIL), Jaipur<br/>(Establishment of 150 AC and 50 DC Charging Stations)	<br/><br/>Recently in the month of January 2019, the proposals received from REIL and BHEL for setting up of Charging Stations at Delhi-Jaipur-Delhi, Mumbai-Pune-Mumbai and Delhi-Chandigarh-Delhi highways have also been sanctioned under FAME India scheme.<br/>	<br/>Under demand creation focus area of the scheme, the purchaser of electric/hybrid vehicle is given an upfront reduction in purchase price by the dealer at the time of purchase of xEV to enable wider adoption. At present, eleven (11) models of electric Two Wheeler of five (5) Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) have registered themselves for availing monetary incentive @ Rs. 22,000/- per vehicle under FAME India Scheme. Similarly, twenty one (21) models of electric Four Wheelers of five (5) OEMs are registered under this scheme for availing monetary incentives @ Rs. 70,000/- , Rs. 1,24,000/- & Rs. 1,38,000/- per vehicle.<br/><br/>***** <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Repatriation of Indian nationals in foreign prisons
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)  	the efforts made by the Ministry to have inter-Ministerial meetings on the repatriation of Indian nationals in foreign prisons; and <br/><br/>(b)  	the details of use of Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF) by Indian Missions for repatriation of Indian prisoners, person-wise and percentage-wise?<br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS<br/>[GEN. (DR) V. K. SINGH (RETD)]<br/><br/>(a)  	There is a regular process of consultation and coordination among relevant Ministries on the issue of repatriation of Indian nationals in foreign prisons including in the context of bilateral agreements for Transfer of Sentenced Persons (TSP).  <br/>	<br/>(b) 	The Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF) is aimed at assisting Indian nationals abroad in times of distress and emergency in the ‘deserving cases’ on a ‘means tested basis’.  In view of its immense utility, ICWF stands extended to all Indian Missions and Posts abroad.<br/><br/>	The revised ICWF guidelines, operational with effect from September 1, 2017, have been made more broad-based and have expanded the scope of welfare measures that can be extended through the Fund. <br/><br/>Since January 2014 – September 2018, over 25000 Indians have been provided air passages from the Fund.  However, separate data related to number of prisoners repatriated through ICWF is not available.<br/><br/>*****

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has data on people who have borrowed and defaulted on a loan of more than 25 crores taken from Public Sector Banks (PSBs);<br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof;<br/>(c)	the details of the total NPAs with PSBs as of December, 2018;<br/>(d)	whether Government envisages stricter checks on loan advances of such large amounts in the future; and<br/>(e)	if so, the details thereof? <br/>
records.ans_text: FINANCE MINISTER<br/><br/><br/> (a) to (e): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>***<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>Statement as referred to in reply to paragraphs (a) to (e) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. *17 for answer on 5th February, 2019/Magha 16, 1940 (Saka) regarding “Loan Defaults in PSBs”, by SHRI SANJAY SETH, Hon’ble Member of Parliament<br/>(a) to (e): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has apprised that as on 30.9.2018, there were 2,043 borrowers with aggregate funded outstanding of Rs. 6,84,824 crore related to Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) of more than Rs. 25 crore outstanding, in respect of Public Sector Banks (PSBs). <br/><br/>As per RBI data on global operations, the aggregate gross advances of PSBs increased from Rs. 18,19,074 crore as on 31.3.2008 to Rs. 52,15,920 crore as on 31.3.2014. As per RBI inputs, the primary reasons for spurt in stressed assets have been observed to be, inter-alia, aggressive lending practices, wilful default / loan frauds / corruption in some cases, and economic slowdown. Asset Quality Review (AQR) initiated in 2015 for clean and fully provisioned bank balance-sheets revealed high incidence of NPAs. As a result of AQR and subsequent transparent recognition by banks, stressed accounts were reclassified as NPAs and expected losses on stressed loans, not provided for earlier under flexibility given to restructured loans, were provided for.  Further, during the financial year 2017-18, all such schemes for restructuring stressed loans were withdrawn. Primarily as a result of transparent recognition of stressed assets as NPAs, gross NPAs of PSBs, as per RBI data on global operations, rose from Rs. 2,79,016 crore as on 31.3.2015, to Rs. 8,95,601 crore as on 31.3.2018, and as a result of Government’s 4R’s strategy of recognition, resolution, recapitalisation and reforms, have since declined to Rs. 8,64,433 crore as on 31.12.2018 (provisional data).<br/>A number of steps have been taken for stricter check on loan advances of large amounts, including, inter alia, the following:<br/>(1)	PSBs have been asked to examine all accounts exceeding Rs. 50 crore, if classified as NPA, from the angle of possible fraud and to immediately initiate examination of the issue of wilful default once a fraud is reported.<br/>(2)	Under the PSB Reforms Agenda announced by the Government,—<br/>(i)	all PSBs have created Stressed Asset Management Verticals, which monitor high-value Special Mention Accounts and identified stressed assets; <br/>(ii)	all PSBs have effected strict segregation of roles and assignment of responsibilities for appraisal, monitoring and recovery in all accounts with outstanding of Rs. 50 crore and above, for clean and effective monitoring;<br/>(iii)	PSBs have committed to monitoring large credit exposures (above Rs. 250 crore) through specialised monitoring agencies; and<br/>(iv)	for ensuring clean corporate lending through rigorous due diligence and appraisal for sanction, PSBs have committed to scrutiny of balance-sheet and ring-fencing of cash flows, use of technology and analytics for comprehensive due-diligence across data sources, and ensuring that necessary clearances are in place and linkages tied up before disbursement.<br/>(3)	Through enactment of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, taking over of management of the affairs of the corporate debtor at the outset of the corporate insolvency resolution process and debarment of wilful defaulters and persons associated with NPA accounts from the process have been provided for, which has instilled greater credit discipline among corporate debtors.  <br/>(4)	PSBs have put in place arrangements for checking credit information reports of Credit Information Companies for sanction and renewal of corporate loans.<br/>(5)	A Central Repository of Information on Large Credits (CRILC) has been created to collect, store and disseminate data on all borrowers’ credit exposures of Rs. 5 crore and above, to enable better monitoring. <br/>(6)	To enable banks to inform relevant authorities if need arises, PSBs have been advised to obtain a certified copy of the passport of promoters/Directors and other authorised signatories of companies availing of loan facilities of more than Rs. 50 crore. <br/>(7)	A Central Fraud Registry has been created for all frauds reported by banks to RBI, involving amount above Rs. 1 lakh. <br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Increase in Taj Mahal ticket price
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that ASI has increased the price of the entry tickets to Taj Mahal from ` 40 to `50 and introduced another charge of `200 for going inside the Mausoleum for Indian tourists; <br/>(b) 	if so, the rationale behind a 200 per cent increase in ticket price; <br/>(c) 	whether Government wants to deter poor Indian tourists from accessing the shared cultural heritage by hiking the tariff; and <br/>(d) 	if not, whether any concession has been planned for poor Indian visitors whereby they can enjoy the Historic Monument at an affordable price?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR TOURISM (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>(SHRI K. J. ALPHONS)<br/><br/><br/>(a):	Yes, Sir. Entry ticket rate has been increased for all monuments vide Gazette Notification S.O. No.1171(E) dated 4.12.2018 issued by Ministry of Culture(ASI), Government of India and an special ticket of Rs. 200/- for entry to main mausoleum of the Taj Mahal has been introduced.<br/><br/>(b):	The decision to introduce a new special entry ticket of Rs. 200/- to enter main mausoleum of the Taj Mahal was taken to restrict tourist inflow and to prevent overcrowding for better security of the monument.<br/><br/>(c):	No, Sir. The above decision was taken to manage the visitor’s flow and the security of the monument/visitors.<br/><br/>(d):	At present, there is no such proposal.<br/><br/>**********<br/>

records.qtitle: Promotion of the musical heritage and the dance forms of Uttar Pradesh
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) 	the efforts being made by Government to promote Kathak as an integral dance form; <br/><br/>(b)	the efforts being made to revive Rasia, Qawalli and Ghazal forms of music endemic to Uttar Pradesh; <br/><br/>(c)	the institutions established, funded, aided by the Government to promote the above;<br/><br/>(d)	whether there exists central scholarships for underprivileged scholars who want to achieve mastery in these fields; and<br/><br/>(e)	the efforts being made on the international fora to promote these cultural heritages?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (IC) FOR CULTURE &<br/>MINISTER OF STATE FOR ENVIRONMENT, FOREST & CLIMATE CHANGE<br/><br/>(DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a):	Ministry of Culture administers a number of scheme components such as Repertory Grants, Cultural Function and Production Grant (CFPG), Financial Assistance to Cultural Organizations with National Presence, Scheme of Scholarship &Fellowship to artists and various cultural fields for promotion of art and culture including Kathak dance.<br/><br/>	Besides, Sangeet Natak Akademi, an autonomous organization under purview of the Ministry of Culture has three constituent units, two of these being institutions teaching dance, viz. the Kathak Kendra in Delhi and Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy at Imphal. Kathak Kendra offers courses at various levels in Kathak dance and in vocal music and Pakhawaj. Kathak Kendra has a Production Unit which strives to enrich the repertoire and technique of Kathak dance through experimental work.<br/><br/>(b)&(c): North Central Zone Cultural Centre (NCZCC), Prayagraj, an autonomous organization under Ministry of Culture has been set up by the Government of India to protect, promote and preserve various forms of folk arts including Rasia. The artists are invited by the NCZCC to showcase this art form in various events organized by them. Annual grant-in-aid is released to NCZCC for carrying out various cultural activities and programmes in its member States.<br/>	Besides, Sangeet Natak Akademi organizes various programmes/festivals to present the artists of Uttar Pradesh to promote Musical Heritage of Uttar Pradesh. Sangeet Natak Akademi has also awarded the musicians/artists by giving National Awards for their contribution to the field of Ghazal, Qawwali and Sufiana Music.<br/><br/>(d):	Sangeet Natak Akademi has constituted a National Scholarship in the field of Ghazal, dedicated to the legendary musician – Begum Akhtar. <br/><br/>(e):	Not yet Sir. <br/>****<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has data on CSR non-compliance by Indian companies;<br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof;<br/>(c)	the steps taken to ensure that CSR funds are actually utilised judiciously; and<br/>(d)	the data on prosecutions undertaken for non compliance with CSR guidelines?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR LAW AND JUSTICE<br/>AND CORPORATE AFFAIRS                                           (SHRI P. P. CHAUDHARY)<br/><br/> (a) to (d) :  Every company having net worth of Rs. 500 crore or more or turnover of Rs. 1000 crore or more or net profit of Rs. 5 crore or more during immediately preceding financial year shall ensure that it spends, in every financial year, at least 2% of the average net profits of the company made during the three immediately financial years, on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities, in areas or subjects specified in Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’). Further the Section 135 (3)&(4) of the Companies Act, 2013 empowers the Board of the Company to take decisions regarding allocation of CSR funds for items listed in Schedule VII of the Act.On scrutiny of data filed by the companies in MCA21 registry under the Companies Act, 2013, the details of CSR expenditure are culled out.Whenever, violation of CSR provision is reported, the Registrar of Companies initiates action against such non-compliant companies. For the FY 2014-15, prosecution against 313 companies were sanctioned out of which 33 companies have filed application for compounding. In addition to this, Ministry has established Centralized Scrutiny and Prosecution Mechanism (CSPM) in April, 2018 for the financial year 2015-16 onwards on pilot basis for enforcement of CSR provisions. Based on scrutiny, preliminary notices have been issued to 5,382 companies for the financial year 2015-16.<br/>********<br/><br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.min_name: WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that Government projects commenced for cleaning of river Ganga have not given desired results; <br/>(b) if so, the reasons therefor; <br/>(c) if not, the details of efforts being made for cleaning the Ganga; and <br/>(d) the plan of Government for cleaning and rejuvenation of the other important rivers?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION & HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. SATYA PAL SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) & (b)  No, Sir. Though the cleaning of river is a continuous process, the actions taken by the government under Namami Gange Programme is resulting in improvement of the river water quality. Under Namami Gange Programme, the Government of India is supplementing the efforts of the State Governments in cleaning the rivers by providing financial assistance. The Central Government approved the ''''Namami Gange Program'''' on 13th May, 2015 with an outlay of Rs 20,000 crore as a comprehensive approach to rejuvenate the river Ganga and its tributaries, under one umbrella, by consolidating the existing ongoing efforts and planning for a concrete action plan for the future.<br/><br/>(c) & (d)  The Namami Gange Programme covers short term, medium term and long term activities. Under short term activities certain entry level activities which cover development of ghats crematoria & river surface cleaning activities etc have been taken up. Under medium term activities, existing Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) and Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs) are being upgraded and new STP & ETPs are being established. Beside, rural sanitation has been taken up in the villages on the banks of river Ganga. The long term action plan involves restoration of wholesomeness of river Ganga and maintaining the ecological & geological integrity of river. The projects under short term activities are on track and are to be completed by March 2019. Under medium and long term activities, variety of coordinated activities meant for cleaning of river Ganga including treatment of municipal sewage, treatment of industrial effluent, drain bio-remediation, river surface cleaning, rural sanitation, river front development, afforestation & biodiversity conservation, public outreach etc. have been taken up. So far, a total of 261 projects have been sanctioned at an estimated cost of Rs.25,563 crore for various activities. Out of these, 76 projects have been completed.<br/>Contd…P/2<br/>//2//<br/>Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF & CC) has been supplementing the efforts of the State Governments in abatement of pollution in identified stretches of various rivers under the centrally sponsored scheme of National River Conservation Plan (NRCP) on cost sharing basis between the Central & State Governments.  Various pollution abatement schemes taken up under NRCP, inter-alia, include interception & diversion of raw sewage, construction of sewerage systems, setting up of sewage treatment plants, low cost sanitation, river front/bathing ghat development, etc.  Implementation of NRCP works has led to reduction in pollution load draining into rivers as well as improving the environmental & sanitation conditions in the towns in which the programmes have been implemented. <br/><br/>NRCP has so far covered polluted stretches of 33 rivers in 76 towns spread over 15 States in the country at a sanctioned cost of Rs.4801.57 crore  and Central share of Rs.2337.73 crore has been released to the State Governments for implementation of various pollution abatement schemes. Sewage treatment capacity of 2520.43 Mld (Million Litres per Day)  has  been created so far under the NRCP.<br/><br/>				The strategies for conservation and rejuvenation of rivers in the country are revised from time to time in consultation with the State Governments and are ongoing processes. Works are taken up in identified polluted river stretches under the National River Conservation Plan on the basis of conformity with the guidelines, pollution status, prioritization, willingness of the State Governments to contribute their matching share and availability of Plan funds and incorporation of appropriate strategies. <br/><br/>******<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Government appointed legislative assistants for MPs
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government is aware that many countries provide MPs with qualified Legislative and Policy Research Assistants for their parliamentary work;<br/><br/>(b)	the reason why our Government does not follow such a scheme;<br/><br/>(c)	if there is a scheme in place, the details thereof ; and <br/><br/>(d)	whether there are plans to staff an MPs office adequately with Research Assistants, to help   him/her discharge his/ her duties in a more informed manner?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION<br/>(SHRI VIJAY GOEL)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (d)	Every country has its own acts and rules to determine the salary and facilities to its people representatives according to their requirements and conditions. The Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 and the Rules made thereunder, which has been enacted in pursuance of constitutional provisions, governs salary and allowances of the Members of Parliament. The Joint Committee of both Houses, which is constituted from time to time, frame rules, after consultation with the Government of India, to provide matters for medical facilities, travelling & daily allowances, housing and telephone facilities, constituency allowance, office expense allowances, etc. The act and the rules made thereunder are amended from time to time in keeping with the changing requirements. As per the Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance), Rules, 1988, Lok Sabha Secretariat/ Rajya Sabha Secretariat may pay up to rupees forty thousand to the person(s) as may be engaged by a Member of Parliament for obtaining secretarial assistance for carrying out the parliamentary work and one such person shall be computer literate duly certified by the Member. <br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether instances of irregularities have been reported in connection with the plantation drives carried out under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act guidelines;<br/>(b)	the details of funds released for Uttar Pradesh under the aforesaid act;<br/>(c)	the details of follow-up action to ascertain the success of such drives; and<br/>(d)	whether GPS technology and Satellite imaging are being used to track the progress of such drives?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE <br/>(DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a)		 The Compensatory Afforestation Fund is utilized for execution of works as per the approved Annual Plan of Operation prepared by State Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority ( CAMPA)  following the State CAMPA Guidelines, 2009. No irregularity has been brought to the notice of Adhoc CAMPA except one case related to Punjab State CAMPA in which Rs. 1,11,24000.00 was used for payments to Lawyers for legal services. The State Government was directed to deposit Rs. 1,11,24000.00 in the CAMPA fund which has been complied by the State Government. <br/><br/>(b)	An amount of Rs. 740.4 crore have been released by the Adhoc CAMPA to State CAMPA Uttar Pradesh for Compensatory Afforestation and other allied activities as per the Annual Plan of Operation approved by the Steering Committee of State CAMPA headed by Chief Secretary of the State. No fund has been released to the State of Uttar Pradesh under Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016,which has come into force from 30th September, 2018.<br/><br/>(c) Third party monitoring and monitoring by State Forest Department are done for activities carried out by State CAMPA.<br/><br/>(d) Yes, an e-Green Watch portal has been developed and the Global Positioning System coordinates of the activities carried out by the State CAMPA are uploaded on this portal by the state forest department, which is monitored on a regular basis. <br/>***<br/><br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has collated data about the high Fluoride levels in drinking water in Uttar Pradesh, if so, the details thereof; <br/>(b) the steps taken for Fluoride removal from hand pumped drinking water in the rural areas; and <br/>(c) details of efforts taken by the National Programme of Prevention and Control of Fluorosis (NPPCF) to aid patients of Fluoride poisoning?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE<br/>IN THE MINISTRY OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION<br/>(SHRI RAMESH CHANDAPPA JIGAJINAGI)<br/><br/>(a) As reported by the Government of Uttar Pradesh in Integrated Management Information System (IMIS) of the Ministry as on 29.01.2019, 178 habitations are affected by fluoride in Uttar Pradesh. <br/><br/>(b) Rural Drinking Water Supply is a State subject. For improving the coverage of safe drinking water to rural population, this Ministry supplements the efforts of the States by providing them with technical and financial assistance through the centrally sponsored scheme; National Rural Drinking Water Programme (NRDWP). It is the State Governments who plan, design, approve, execute, operate & maintain the schemes for providing safe drinking water to rural population. The funds provided to the States under NRDWP can be utilized for providing safe drinking water to water quality affected areas on priority.<br/><br/>(c) As reported by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, 156 districts of 19 States have been covered under the National Programme of Prevention and Control of Fluorosis (NPPCF) Programme. The State-wise list of districts under the programme is at Annexure.<br/><br/>Support provided at district level by Ministry of Health & Family Welfare through NPPCF programme is as follows:-<br/>•	Strengthening manpower in endemic districts by providing for: Consultant (1), Laboratory Technician (1), Field Investigators (3) for six months. <br/>•	Purchase of equipment for lab including an Ion meter for water and urinary analysis of fluoride levels. <br/>•	Training of medical and paramedical workers at various levels. <br/>•	Health Education and Publicity (IEC). <br/>•	Supplementation with vitamins and minerals and treatment including reconstructive surgery and rehabilitation of Fluorosis affected patients.<br/><br/>******<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Feeding excess solar energy into grid
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether there is a provision for pumping the excess solar energy produced by any institution or household back into the grid for distribution;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details of the energy received from such a feed in system nationally;<br/><br/>(c) the procedure to avail of such facility; and<br/><br/>(d) the statistics of Central Government offices that have contributed to the scheme?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER (I/C)<br/>(SHRI R. K. SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) to (d) Yes sir. The regulations notified by respective State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs) provide for feeding surplus solar power generated by rooftop solar projects into the grid.<br/><br/>This facility can be availed by any eligible consumer by applying to the respective distribution utility as per provisions of the regulations notified by respective SERCs.<br/><br/>The surplus solar power from rooftop solar projects is fed back to the grid as distribution level and consumed at distribution level, and therefore, is not accounted in the national system.<br/><br/>As reported on SPIN portal of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, a total of the 221.79 MW capacity rooftop solar power plants have been installed in the Government offices till 31.12.2018.<br/><br/>*****

records.qtitle: Development of sports in Uttar Pradesh
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) the number of sports complexes established or fully funded by Government in the State of Uttar Pradesh;<br/>(b) the statistics regarding the major International achievements in sports from the State of Uttar Pradesh;<br/>(c) the details of financial aid to sportspersons from underprivileged background; and<br/>(d) initiatives taken by Government to promote sports at village and block levels?
records.ans_text: VTHE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>FOR YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS<br/>{COL. RAJYAVARDHAN RATHORE (RETD.)}<br/><br/>(a) to (d) Sports is a State subject and promotion of sports in the country, including creation of sports infrastructure in States is primarily the responsibility of the State Government concerned. The Central Government complements/supplements the efforts of the State Governments.<br/>This Ministry is implementing the Khelo India Scheme which inter-alia includes a vertical „Utilisation and Creation/ Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure? which provides for grant of financial assistance for filling the critical gaps in sports infrastructure of the country including Uttar Pradesh. Details of sports infrastructure sanctioned in the State of Uttar Pradesh under Khelo India Scheme is given at Annexure.<br/>National level and International level competitions are organized by concerned National Sports Federations (NSFs) / National Olympic Committees in association with their world body. The participation in such tournaments are through these organizations. The Government does not have a direct role in the same. Accordingly, this Ministry does not maintain State-wise details of achievements of sports persons in international events.<br/>The Khelo India scheme has a dedicated vertical “Talent Search and Development” which provides for financial assistance at the rate of Rs.5.00 lakh per annum, for a period of 8 years, to identified talented players in priority sports disciplines. The scheme caters to the entire population also covering sportspersons from underprivileged background across the country and 1518 sportspersons have been identified (upto 07.12.2018) for support under the Scheme.<br/>Sports Authority of India (SAI), an autonomous organization under the aegis of the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, is implementing a number of sports promotional schemes across the country to identify talented sports persons in the age group of 8-25 years and nurture them to excel at national and international competitions. Many of the sports persons identified under SAI Sports Promotional Schemes belong to the rural, tribal, backward, coastal and inaccessible hilly areas of the country and are provided with training facilities in the form of expert sports coaches, requisite playing facilities, boarding & lodging, sports kit, competition exposure, educational expenses, medical/insurance and stipend as per the approved norms.<br/>******

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: <br/>(a)	whether it is a fact that every year more than ten lakh people in India die due to air pollution only;<br/>(b)	if so, the steps taken by Government to check air pollution; and <br/>(c)	if not, the level of pollution in India and annual death rate due to it?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE <br/><br/>(DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a)& (c) There is no conclusive data available in the country to establish direct correlation of death/disease exclusively due to air pollution. Air pollution is one of the triggering factors for respiratory ailments and associated diseases. Health effects of air pollution are synergistic manifestation of factors which include food habits, occupational habits, socio-economic status, medical history, immunity, heredity, etc., of the individuals.<br/><br/>The Government has however, taken several steps to address air pollution, which inter alia include notification of National Ambient Air Quality Standards; revision of emission standards for industrial sectors from time to time; setting up of monitoring network for assessment of ambient air quality; introduction of cleaner / alternate fuels like gaseous fuel (CNG, LPG etc.), ethanol blending, launching of National Air Quality index; leapfrogging from BS-IV to BS-VI fuel standards; notification of Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules; banning of burning of biomass;  streamlining the issuance of Pollution Under Control Certificate;  issuance of directions under Section 18(1)(b) of Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and under Section 5 of Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 for controlling air pollution; installation of on-line continuous (24x7) monitoring devices by major industries; notification of Graded Response Action Plan for Delhi and NCR; comprehensive action plan for air pollution control in Delhi and NCR; etc. <br/><br/>*********<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: a)  whether in the  latest International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) audit results, India''s score declined to 57.44 percent from 65.82 per cent earlier;<br/><br/>(b) if so, what measures have been taken to make aviation safer and perform better in the upcoming audit; and<br/><br/>(c) what parameters are country lacking in according to the ICAO audit?<br/>
records.ans_text: The Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Jayant Sinha)<br/><br/>(a) ICAO conducted an audit of India in November 2015 and November 2017 wherein the Effective Implementation (EI) was 57.44%. Based on the recent audit conducted by ICAO in November 2018 covering areas of Legislation, Organisation, Air Navigation Services, Aerodromes and Accident Investigation, the EI has raised to approximately 73.6%.<br/><br/>(b) & (c) The lack of regulation and oversight of Air Traffic Controllers resulted in India''s low score in the ICAO Audit of November 2017. In pursuance of the observations made by ICAO in their audit report, it has been decided that the regulation and oversight of Air Traffic Controllers will be done by Directorate General of Civil Aviation.<br/>

records.qtitle: Plateform used for fifty nine minute loan for MSMEs
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	what is the platform used to process the application for the fifty nine minute loan for the MSME sector announced by Government;<br/>(b)	whether the online application portal is run by Government or a private enterprise, the details thereof;<br/>(c)	the details of the process followed to select the portal operator along with details of participating entities in the selection process;<br/>(d)	the amount charged by the loan portal for each application made on it; and<br/>(e)	the number of applications made on the portal as per latest available data and against the list of loans sanctioned and disbursed to applicants?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/><br/><br/>(a) & (b)Loans in 59 minutes for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector are facilitated through www.psbloansin59minutes.com, an online lending portal run by “Online PSB Loans Limited”, a public limited company wherein 6 Public Sector Banks (PSBs) and Financial Institutions(FIs) along with their associate companies hold 54% majority stake and majority seats ( 4 out of 7 ) on the Board.<br/>(c)  After exploring alternative options, a group of bankers from Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) and PSBs opted for acquisition of majority stake in an existing financial technology (Fintech) company to achieve desired objectives of a near ready platform and operational team within desired timelines. A multi stage selection and filtering process was carried out involving SIDBI and PSBs to select the FinTech with desired capabilities. This was followed by third party audit(s) and validation at various stages, through reputed external entities. PSBs, FIs and their associate companies thereafter made their own assessments prior to making investments. <br/>(d)  No fee is charged from borrowers for registration of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) on the portal or for cases of renewal. Convenience Charge of Rs.1000/- + GST is levied only when the MSME gets in-principle approval on the marketplace Uniform Resource Locator(URL) of the portal.The charge collected is used by Online PSB Loans Ltd. to meet out of pocket expenses payable to third parties for various services and for its own expenditure.<br/>(e)  As on 25.12.2018, out of 1,31,028 completed applications received on the portal, 1,12,043 applications for loans have been accorded in- principle approval. Sanctions have been made in respect of 40,669 cases.<br/>*** <br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether consultations were undertaken with stakeholders before deciding on the New Pension Scheme (NPS); <br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof; <br/>(c)	whether it is a fact that the NPS is equity oriented, thereby making monthly pension highly contingent upon market conditions; and <br/>(d)	what social security measures have been taken to ensure a sustainable minimum pension delivery<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: <br/><br/>The Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance    <br/><br/><br/>(a) and (b) Government had made a conscious move to shift from the defined benefit pension scheme to defined contribution pension scheme i.e. National Pension System (NPS) due to rising and unsustainable pension bill. The Government of India vide notification dated 22.12.2003 had introduced the National Pension System (NPS) (earlier known as New Pension Scheme) for its employees and made it mandatory for all new recruits of the Central Government (excluding armed forces) who joined service on or after 01.01.2004.<br/>(c) NPS is market-linked retirement product. The investment under NPS is made in various asset classes including Government Securities, Corporate Debt instruments and equities as per the investment guidelines issued by Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) in this regard, out of these the investment in equity is up to maximum 15% only. <br/>(d) The Government has recently approved proposals for streamlining the NPS and to ensure a sustainable minimum pension delivery. The measures are as follows:<br/>i.	Enhancement of the mandatory contribution by the Central Government for Tier I accounts of its employees covered under NPS from the existing 10% to 14%. The employees’ contribution rate would remain at the existing 10%. <br/>ii.	Providing freedom of choice for selection of Pension Funds and pattern of investment to central government employees.<br/>iii.	Tax exemption limit for lump sum withdrawal on exit has been enhanced to 60%. With this, the entire withdrawal will now be exempt from income tax.<br/>*********<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that Government has decided not to grant disability pension to officers of Armed Forces who have opted for Voluntary retirement;<br/><br/><br/>(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and <br/><br/>(c) if not, by when this pension would be granted to them?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF DEFENCE<br/>DR. SUBHASH BHAMRE<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c):  As per Ministry of Defence order dated 31.01.2001, Armed Forces Personnel who retire voluntarily / or seek discharge on request are not eligible for any award on account of disability.  Provided that Armed Forces Personnel who are due for retirement / discharge on completion of tenure, or on completion of service limits, or on completion of the terms of engagement or on attaining the prescribed age of retirement, and who seeks pre-mature retirement / discharge on request for the purpose of getting higher commutation value of pension will remain eligible for disability element.<br/><br/>         Further, Armed Forces personnel who are retained in service despite disability, which is accepted as attributable to or aggravated by Military Service and have forgone lump sum compensation in lieu of that disability, may be given disability element / war injury element at the time of their retirement / discharge whether voluntary or otherwise in addition to Retiring / Service Pension or Retiring / Service Gratuity.  These provisions are effective from 1.1.2006.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	the step being taken by Government to improve the quality of 	legal education in the country;<br/><br/>(b)	whether there exists guidelines to declare a Law University 	as  National Law University(NLU), if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c)	whether any Law colleges/Universities in the Country have 	been bestowed the tag of “Institutes of National Importance” or        or  	“Institutes of Eminence”;<br/><br/>(d)	if so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(e)	if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/><br/>MINISTER OF LAW & JUSTICE AND ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY<br/>(SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD)<br/><br/> (a) to (e)	A statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/>******<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>STATEMENT REFFERED TO IN RESPECT OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. *178 DATED 28, DECEMBER, 2018<br/><br/> (a): The Bar Council of India has framed Rules of Legal Education, 2008 under the power conferred by the Advocates Act, 1961. The Law Commission of India submitted its 266th report to Government of India in March 2017 titled “The Advocates Act, 1961 (Regulation of Legal Profession)” in which it has made various recommendations to improve standards of legal education in India. <br/> (b) : Bar Council of India has informed that there are no guideline/s to declare any university or institution as National Law University. Moreover, National Law Universities, which have been established and are in existence today, are all creation of statutes of the State Government and are also run by the respective State Governments.<br/><br/> (c) to (e): The entry 64 of list-I of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India provides that “Institutions for scientific or technical education financed by the Government of India wholly or in part and declared by Parliament by law to be institutions of national importance”. At present no Law Colleges/Universities in the country have been bestowed the tag of “Institutes of National Importance” or “Institutes of Eminence”.<br/>

records.qtitle: Allowing access to foreign law firms
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government is aware of the dismal working conditions prevailing in prominent law firms in the country;<br/><br/>(b)	Whether there are any laws regulating working hours in the legal sector;<br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(d)	whether government plans to allow foreign legal firms to access the Indian legal market by amending the Advocates Act; and <br/><br/>(e)	if so, the details thereof, if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/><br/>MINISTER OF STATE FOR LAW AND JUSTICE AND CORPORATE AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI P.P. CHAUDHARY)<br/><br/>(a) Bar Council of India has stated that they have not received any major complaint relating to working conditions prevailing in prominent law firms in the country.  However they have received some  complaints  from a few litigants over fees being taken by some firms and work not having been done in lieu of fees  etc.<br/>(b) &(c) There are no rules of Bar Council of India regulating working hours in the legal sector. The profession of advocacy requires hard work  by advocates and so the amount of working hours put in by an advocate in a case depends on a variety of factors including complexity of the issue <br/><br/><br/>involved in the case, support provided by client in the form of relevant materials etc.  <br/><br/>(d)& (e) The Law Commission of India Submitted its 266th report titled “The Advocates Act,1961 (Regulation of Legal Profession)” to Government of India in March 2017 on the issue of entry of Foreign Law Firms. The Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 13.03.2018 in  Civil Appeal Nos.7875-7879 of  2015  titled Bar Council of  India Vs A.K. Balaji and Ors. has held that foreign law firms cannot set up offices in India or practice in Indian Courts, but there is no bar for the foreign law firms or foreign lawyers to visit India for a temporary period for giving legal advice regarding foreign law on diverse international legal issues on a ‘fly in and fly out’ basis if it does not amount to practice. It was further held that if the matter is governed by particular rules of an arbitral institution or if the matter otherwise falls under section 32 or 33 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 there is no bar on foreign lawyers to conduct such proceedings in India.  Even in such cases, Code of Conduct, if any, applicable to the legal profession in India has to be followed. It is for the Bar Council of India or Central Government to make a specific provision in this regard, if considered appropriate. Hon’ble Supreme Court judgment dated 13.03.2018 and 266th report of Law Commission of India are under consideration of Government of India. <br/>

records.qtitle: Production of coal by re allocated coal mines
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that less than 15 of the 33 coal mines re-allocated in 2014 have started production, if so, the reasons<br/>therefor;<br/> <br/>(b) whether such a long delay is attributable to bureaucratic lethargy and lengthy clearance processes;<br/> <br/>(c) whether it is also a fact that the country had to import 10 per cent the total domestic coal demand in the current fiscal despite having adequate reserves, and<br/> <br/>(d) the steps being taken by Government to plug the shortfall and cut down on import dependency? <br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>         MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND COAL<br/>     (SHRI PIYUSH GOYAL)<br/>  <br/>(a)&(b) Out of 85 coal blocks allocated under Coal Mine(Special Provisions) Act’ 2015(33 are Schedule II mines,18 Schedule I mines & 34 Schedule III mines), 24 mines are presently operational which includes 17 mines under Schedule II category and balance 7 mines under Schedule I & III. Out of these 24 operational mines, 16 mines are coal producing mines of which 13 are Schedule II mines.<br/> <br/>The Milestones are mentioned in the Schedule-E of CMPDA (Coal Mine Production and Development Agreement), where time lines are present for the clearances required. In case of Schedule-II coal mines, all the clearances were in place & it was expected that it would be transferred to new allottee in 3 months but mainly due to the change in Land status/ existing Law, it did not happen. The following issues were identified as the major reasons for non-operationalization /delay in operationalization of coal mines:<br/> <br/>•	Procedural delay in transfer of clearances existing with Prior allottees like ECs, FCs and Mining Leases.<br/>•	Litigation related to land.<br/>•	Processes are not standard across states that added to delays.<br/><br/>However, due to close monitoring by the Ministry, the total coal production from these blocks has been 14.71 MT during April-November 2018 at a growth rate of 34.70 % over the same period last year.<br/> <br/>(c) &(d) The all India demand of coal, production, supply and import of coal  during last two years and current year i.e. 2018 upto November 2018 is given below:<br/> <br/>Year	2016-17	2017-18	2018-19<br/>Total demand (Mte) ^	884.87	908.40	991.35<br/>Total domestic Production (Mte)	657.87	676.48	433.90@<br/>Total domestic supply (Mte)	644.56	691.42	471.70@<br/>Total Import (Mte)	190.95	208.27	111.60#<br/>^All India Estimated by NitiAayog ; @Upto November, 2018; # upto September,2018<br/> <br/>The imported coal quantity of 2017-18 at 208.27 MT is less than the imported quantity of 2014-15 which stood at 217.79 MT even as power generation and industrial activities grew substantially after 2014-15.<br/> <br/> As per the current import policy, coal is kept under Open General License (OGL) and consumers are free to import coal from the source of their choice as per their contractual prices on payment of applicable duty. There has been a consistent effort to increase domestic coal production so as to reduce dependence on coal imports. The all India raw coal production has increased from 565.77 MT in 2013-14 to 676.48 MT in 2017-18. Absolute increase in all India coal production from 2013-14 to 2017-18( four years) is 110.71 Mt as compared to increase of coal production of 33.73 MT from 2009-10 to 2013-14( four years).<br/> <br/>Coal India Limited (CIL) has also increased its production from 462.41 MT in 2013-14 to 567.36 MT in 2017-18(four years), an absolute increase of 105 MT as compared to increase of coal production of 31.15 MT between 2009-10 and 2013-14 (four years). Further, in the current year during April-November, 2018 all India coal production was 433.90 MT with a growth rate of 9.8% and coal production of CIL was 358.32 Mt with a growth rate of 8.8% over the corresponding period of previous year.<br/> <br/>To reduce import dependence and facilitate the Power consumers for procuring coal under Special Forward E-Auction, CIL has planned to offer about 41.54 MT of coal in 2018-19. During Apr-Sep 2018, around 27.68MT coal was offered under Special Forward E-Auction by different coal companies against which around 20.38 MT coal was booked by Power consumers.<br/>For Non-regulated sector, CIL is conducting linkage auctions for Sponge Iron, Cement, CPP, ‘Other (non-coking)’, Steel (coking) and ‘Others (coking)’ sub sectors under Non- Regulated Sector. In the three tranches of linkage auction which have been concluded, 45.18 MT of annual col linkages have been booked. In the fourth tranche, up to now, 26.54 MT of annual coal linkages have been booked by CPP, Cement and Sponge Iron Sector consumers. For linkages of coking coal, CIL has offered a total quantity of 6.99MT in the linkage auctions against which only 0.22 MT has been booked by Steel sector consumers.<br/> <br/>However, coking coal will continue to be imported as there is limited availability of coking coal in the country. Further, power plants designed on imported coal will also continue to import coal.<br/> <br/>***<br/> <br/><br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)  what measures have been taken for the education and mental development of children affected with autism; <br/>      (b) whether there are any special institutions run by Government specifically for children affected with autism;<br/>      (c) whether there are care institutions/assisted living centers for such children and the provisions for sustenance allowance to their legal guardians; and<br/>      (d)  If so, the details thereof?        <br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT <br/>(SHRI KRISHANPAL GURJAR)<br/><br/>(a)	: The National Trust for the welfare of persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation & Multiple Disabilities is implementing an early intervention and school readiness scheme named ‘Disha’ for education and mental development of children affected with Autism.  The Scheme has provisions for setting up of early intervention centres in selected registered organization centres of the National Trust.  Training on early intervention and school readiness programme is given to children of 0 to 10 years age group.  Parents of these children are also trained to carry out these activities at home.<br/><br/>(b)	: The National Trust implements Disha (early intervention and school readiness) Scheme through its registered organizations at 58 places in the country.<br/><br/>(c) to (d): The National Trust, through its registered organizations, implements a respite care residential scheme named ‘Samarth’ for such children at 20 places in the country. List of Samarth Centres is annexed. The objective of the scheme is to provide respite home for orphans, abandoned, destitute, families in crisis and also for Below Poverty Line (BPL) and Low Income Group (LIG) persons affected with autism. The scheme also aims at creating opportunities for family members to get respite time in order to fulfill other responsibilities. The scheme has provision for home facility for all age groups of Divyangjan covered under the National Trust Act. A Samarth Centre can accommodate upto 30 Divyangjan. There is, however, no provision for sustenance allowance to their legal guardians under any scheme of the National Trust.<br/><br/>****<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the Indian passport ranks a dismal 67 out of 94 in the global passport index below Ghana, Mongolia, Botswana, Lesotho, Kazakhstan and others;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the reasons therefor;<br/><br/>(c) 	the details of countries where Indian citizens could visit visa free or on visa on arrival basis;<br/><br/>(d) 	the details of countries that enjoy visa free/visa on arrival facilities in India;<br/><br/>(e) 	whether such an arrangement is on a reciprocal basis; and<br/><br/>(f) 	if not, the reasons therefor and the steps taken to increase the acceptability of the Indian passport abroad?<br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS<br/>[GEN. (DR) V. K. SINGH (RETD)]<br/><br/>(a) to (c)		As per the information available on www.passportindex.org, the Arton Capital Passport Index (ACPI) gives global ranking to various passports based on the "visa free” status accorded to the passport holders of a specific country. The current passport ranking is based on the number of countries a passport holder can visit Visa Free or gets Visa on Arrival. To determine the individual rank of each passport, a Visa Free Score (VFS) is prepared which is the sum of Visa Free (VF) and Visa on Arrival (VoA) facility accorded to the passport holder of a country.<br/><br/>As per the ACPI, India is ranked 67th as on 22 December, 2018 with a VFS of 65; 25 countries according VF entry and 40 countries granting VOA facility to Indian passport holders. India was ranked 73rd in 2017 with a VFS of 57 with 25 countries according VF entry and 32 countries granting VOA facility to Indian passport holders. The details are at Annexure – I & II..<br/><br/>(d) 	The countries that enjoy visa free facility in India are Bhutan and Nepal and this is on reciprocal basis. The countries which enjoy visa on arrival facilities in India are Japan and Republic of Korea. <br/><br/>(e) & (f)		Extension of Visa on Arrival and Visa free Entry is a unilateral decision of the receiving country. The Government has, however, been continuously liberalizing the visa policy with the objective of promoting investments and tourism into India from other countries. The e-Visa scheme has been further liberalized to allow business visits and medical treatment in India. The number of entries and validity of e-Visas has been increased and the scheme has been expanded to include 166 countries and territories till date. These initiatives are expected to encourage other countries to reciprocate and facilitate travel of Indian passport holders to their countries. As more countries permit Indian passport holders to visit Visa Free or grant them Visa on Arrival facility, the rank of the Indian passport on the Global Passport Index is expected to improve. <br/>*****

records.qtitle: Action against telecom companies for call drops
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that inspite of increasing complaints of call drops by consumers, Government is not taking any action against telecom companies; <br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the reasons therefor; and <br/><br/>(c) 	if not, the directions of Government to telecom companies regarding providing services and the names of the companies against whom action has been taken?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS &<br/> MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/>(SHRI MANOJ SINHA)<br/><br/>(a) to (c)        Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has been interacting with Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) and reviewing the progress of their action-plans for addressing call drops in their mobile networks on a continuous basis.<br/><br/>In order to address call drops, the following steps have been taken:<br/><br/>(i)	DoT has taken several policy initiatives to facilitate infrastructure growth for delivery of quality services. These include permitting trading/sharing/ liberalisation of spectrum already granted, permitting passive & active infrastructure sharing, notification of Right of Way Rules 2016, making available government land/buildings for installation of towers etc.<br/><br/>(ii)	About 9.74 lakh additional BTS for 2G/3G/4G-LTE services have been added by TSPs since July 2015, taking the total BTS count in the country to about 20.07 lakh in November 2018.<br/><br/>(iii)	In order to obtain direct feedback from subscribers, DoT has launched an Interactive Voice Response System (IVRS) wherein, around 2.15 Crore subscribers have been individually contacted since December 2016, out of which 30.1 lakh subscribers have participated in the survey. The feedback is shared with the TSPs every week for taking corrective actions in a time bound manner. As a result, about 85,000 individual cases of call drops have been resolved so far.<br/><br/>	As a result of continuous efforts, significant improvement has been observed in terms of TSPs’ compliance to Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Quality of Services benchmarks on call-drop rate in spite of rapid-increase in traffic volume and more stringent TRAI benchmarks effective from 1st October 2017. TSPs are mostly complying to these benchmarks.<br/><br/>Since 1st October 2017, TRAI has also introduced a revised graded Financial Disincentives (FD) structure based on the extent to which a TSP’s performance deviates from the specified call-drop benchmark(s). Accordingly, the financial disincentives imposed on non-compliant TSPs are given at Annexure-I.<br/>

records.qtitle: Skill development programme and job opportunities
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that those receiving training under skill development programme are also finding it difficult to get a job;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(c)	if not, the number of persons who have received training under the skill development programme since its inception to till date number of persons who were able to secure employment following this training, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>(a) to (c)	Under Skill India Mission, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship is implementing a flagship scheme known as Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) with an objective to provide skilling to one crore people under Short Term Training (STT), Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and Special Project (SP) across the country for four years i.e. 2016-2020. Training under PMKVY 2016-20 is being imparted in National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF) aligned Job Roles. <br/><br/>Under Skilling eco-system, Ministry is promoting employer participation in order to facilitate placement of the trained candidates under various sectors. Further, employers are actively participating as training partner/centre in training- cum- placement activities of the candidates. Also, scheme incentivises Training Centers (TCs) for facilitating placement of the trained candidates. TCs are mandated to organize Placement / Rozgar Melas every six months with support from the Sector Skill Councils (SSCs) and to ensure participation of local industry. Additionally, post placement support of Rs. 1450 per month per trainee is applicable for special group (women candidates and persons with disability) and special areas for 2 or 3 month post training depending on placement within or outside the district of the domicile of the candidate. <br/><br/>Under the PMKVY 2016-20 scheme, as on 30.11.2018, 33.93 lakh (appx.) candidates have been trained under STT (24.13 lakh), RPL (9.08 lakh) and Special Project (0.72 lakh) across the country in various sector. PMKVY 2016-20 scheme has mandatory provisions for placement tracking. The placement data is reported within 90 days of certification of trained candidates on the Skill Development Management System (SDMS). As per data reported on SDMS, as on 30.11.2018, 20.18 lakh candidates have been certified under Short Term Training of PMKVY 2016-20. The number of candidates certified under Short Term Training of PMKVY 90 days prior i.e. 31.08.2018 is 18.42 lakh. Out of these candidates, as on 30.11.2018, 10.09 lakh candidates have been reported placed in various sectors across the country.
