records.qtitle: Extension of PMKVY to jail inmates
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) has been extended to jail inmates lodged in different Central Jails;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, details thereof;<br/><br/>(c)	number of jail inmates who have been enrolled and trained in various trades during last two years;<br/><br/>(d)	amount allocated for training of jail inmates during last two years;<br/><br/>(e)	whether Government has taken steps for placement of jail inmates after obtaining skill development training;<br/><br/>(f)	if so, the State-wise details thereof for the last two years; and<br/><br/>(g)	the other steps taken by Government to train more jail inmates with the help of State Governments, industry and other voluntary organizations?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) to (g)	“Prisons” is a State subject as per the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India and management of jails, including skilling of inmates is primarily the responsibility of the States. However, training of prisoners in various vocational skills has received a lot of importance in almost all the States/Union Territories and these programmes are organized by the jail authorities with the help of State Government/industry/other voluntary organizations from time to time.<br/><br/>Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana is not aimed specifically for a group/ gender or geography but aims to bring in the fold of skilling everyone across the country including the jail inmates. Special Projects under PMKVY is specifically designed to facilitate outreach to various marginalized, vulnerable, socially disadvantaged, hidden and hard-to-reach population of the society. Under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 2015-16, 851 inmates (who have only a balance of 6 months time before release) of Tihar Jail, Delhi were enrolled and trained in a range of trades including Beauty and Wellness, Retail, Data Entry Operator, Electrician, Hospitality, Telecom, Customer Care Executive, Sewing Machine Operator etc. through two training partners of National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC). Further, under PMKVY 2016-20, training allocation of 1880 has been done for Sunaria Jail Rohtak, Central Prison- Rajahmahendravaram and Tihar Jail-Delhi. <br/><br/>The Project Implement Agencies (PIAs) for both ongoing and approved projects have committed to primarily enhancing the income of the jail inmates through market linkages and   commitments to source the items produced by the jail inmates. <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Losses to PNB due to fraud
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether State-run lender Punjab National Bank (PNB) has reported unauthorised transaction worth Rs. 11,500 crore in one of its branches in South Mumbai which is one of the biggest frauds in the Indian banking system; <br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof and quantum of loss to PNB; <br/><br/>(c)	whether guilty persons have been arrested, if so, the details thereof;  <br/><br/>(d)	 whether Government has constituted any inquiry in the matter;<br/><br/>(e)	 if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(f)	 number of employees who have been found guilty and action taken against them; and<br/><br/>(g)	 other steps taken by Government to check and stop such type of unauthorised transactions?    <br/>
records.ans_text: The Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance<br/><br/>(a) and (b): As per Reserve Bank of India (RBI) inputs, Punjab National Bank (PNB) reported fraudulent issuance of Letters of Undertaking / Foreign Letters of Credit for payments of import bills and fraudulent transactions in borrowal accounts, amounting to Rs. 12,967.86 crore, to RBI through its Fraud Monitoring Reporting System. PNB has informed that the loss may not be ascertainable at present as the matter is under investigation. <br/><br/><br/>(c) to (e): The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)  and PNB have apprised that CBI has registered three cases relating to unauthorised transactions at PNB, and several persons have been arrested. The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has apprised that, on the basis of FIRs registered by CBI, it has conducted searches at various locations, which resulted in seizure of valuables, and that it has also attached immovable properties and frozen mutual funds and bank accounts. ED has further apprised that Letter of Request to 13 countries have been issued by the court, seeking details of properties, bank accounts of companies, etc., and that ED has obtained non-bailable warrants against two defaulters. Investigation is in progress. <br/><br/>Ministry of External Affairs has apprised that all passports of two defaulters have been revoked/cancelled by the passport authorities, as per passport rules. <br/><br/>(f): As per CBI inputs, eight public servants belonging to PNB had been arrested. PNB has placed 21 officers/employees under suspension, and stated that action shall be taken against staff found guilty on the basis of investigation report. <br/><br/>(g): RBI has issued instructions mandating banks to implement, within stipulated deadlines, prescribed measures for strengthening the SWIFT operating environment in banks. Further, it has constituted an Expert Committee to look into, inter alia, factors leading to increasing incidence of frauds in banks and the measures (including information technology interventions) needed to curb and prevent it, and the role and effectiveness of various types of audits conducted in banks in mitigating the incidence of such frauds. <br/><br/>Government has issued an advisory to nationalised banks to take immediate action as per extant legal/regulatory framework to ensure that such/similar fraudulent activity (as reported by PNB) is not prevalent in the bank. They have also been asked to ensure that robust systems and procedures are in place for confirming due approvals, necessary applications/documents and entry in the bank’s system in respect of all Letters of Undertakings/Comfort and SWIFT messages, and ensuring scrutiny and reconciliation of Nostro accounts, and to take all necessary steps to safeguard against occurrence of such frauds. Government has further advised nationalised banks to collectively prepare a report for effective management of operational risks, including technology risk, so as to safeguard against occurrence of frauds. <br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: BLAST ON DRILLING SHIP AT COCHIN SHIPYARD LTD.
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether a blast on board of an under repair drilling ship at Cochin Shipyard Ltd.<br/>in Kerala has taken place recently;<br/>(b) 	if so, the number of persons injured dead in the incident;<br/>(c) 	the amount of compensation extended to families of those killed and injured in the incident;<br/>(d) 	whether Government has constituted a high level inquiry into the accident;<br/>(e) 	if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(f) 	the steps taken/being taken by Government to avoid such incidence in the future?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: (a)&(b):Yes, Sir. Five lives were lost and nine persons were injured. <br/><br/>(c)	The details of compensation paid/being paid to the injured and the family of deceased persons are as follows : (A) for the deceased: (i) to the family, Rs. 10 Lakhs, in addition to the statutory compensation and insurance relief as applicable to them; (ii) appropriate employment on compassionate grounds to any eligible dependant of the deceased; (iii) appropriate financial aid towards the education of the children of the deceased, up to and including graduate level; and (iv) to enable the families to defray the expenses related to the funeral and other rituals, Rs. 25,000/- disbursed on the day itself and (B) for the injured:  (i) all treatment expenses incurred for the injured; (ii) amount equivalent to 2 months normal wages to the injured disbursed immediately; and (iii) in addition to the statutory compensation relief, Company to disburse wages to the injured till they return to work.<br/><br/>(d)&(e):Yes, Sir. A high level enquiry into the incident was ordered by the Chairman and Managing Director, CSL under the Chairmanship of Director (Operations) of CSL to investigate into the matter and bring out the root cause of the incident and possible ways of avoiding such incidents in future. Chief General Manager (Technical & Infra), Chief General Manager (Inspection and Quality Control, Health Safety and Environment) and Assistant General Manager and Chief Safety Officer are members of the Committee. <br/><br/>(f)    Certain immediate actions have been taken, which include fresh procurement of personnel safety/protective equipment, escalating workers awareness on Health Safety Environment (HSE) and issuing/displaying of safety alerts more frequently and prominently. Further systemic improvements, if any required, will also be implemented based on the outcome of the enquiry.<br/>*****<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has decided to launch a dedicated air pollution abatement programme; <br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof including the aims and objective; <br/>(c) 	the number of cities to be covered under this programme;<br/>(d) 	the criteria fixed by Government to select cities for this programme; <br/>(e) 	whether Government has set any target to reduce pollution level in these cities; <br/>(f)	if so, the details thereof; and <br/>(g) 	other steps taken by Government to achieve the target fixed under National Clean Air Programme?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE <br/><br/>(DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a)& (b)The government has formulated National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) as a long term time bound national level strategy to tackle the increasing air pollution problem across the country in comprehensive manner. The overall objective is comprehensive management plan for prevention, control and abatement of air pollution besides augmenting and evolving effective ambient air quality monitoring network across the country. The NCAP focuses on collaborative and participatory approach comprising all sources of pollution and coordination between relevant Central Ministries, State Governments, local bodies and other stakeholders.<br/><br/>(c)& (d) Hundred (100) non-attainment cities have been selected for implementation of NCAP. These non- attainment cities have been identified by Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) on the basis of ambient air quality data obtained (2011-2015) under National Air Quality Monitoring Programme (NAMP)and in which the prescribed National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) are violated continuously for five years.<br/><br/>(e)to (g) In addition to formulation of city section action plans, the NCAP has many additional peripheral components viz. Technical Assessment Cell, sharing of international best practices, awareness and capacity building, source apportionment studies, plantation drive etc to support the time bound implementation of these action plans<br/>****<br/><br/>

records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI UPENDRA KUSHWAHA)<br/>*****<br/>(a)	Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) hasbeen providing Tele-Counselling	facility to the students and parents of the CBSE affiliated schools since 1998. records.qtitle: Meeting of Council for Trade Development and Promotion
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has recently organized third meeting of the Council for Trade Development and Promotion; <br/>(b)	if so, details thereof along with number of States that have participated in the meeting;<br/>(c)	whether in the meeting Central Government has proposed incentives for States which play a proactive role in promoting exports; <br/>(d)	whether the Central Government has also asked States to appoint at least one nodal officer at district level which is the closest to the local market, if so, response of the State Government thereto; and <br/>(e)	the other steps taken by Government to promote overall exports and push the country''s industrial growth?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY <br/> (SHRI C. R. CHAUDHARY) <br/><br/>(a) & (b) Yes, Sir.  The 3rd Meeting of the Council for Trade Development and Promotion was held on 08th January, 2018 in New Delhi under the Chairmanship of Hon''ble Commerce & Industry Minister in which representatives from 28 states and 4 UTs participated including 13 Ministers. The State/UT representatives articulated their perspective on the trade policy, the need for creating more awareness about export related issues and resolved to jointly address impediments in trade which affect India’s exports. The major issues discussed were promoting services exports, organic farming, value addition to agricultural products including facilitation for branding, promotion, packing and developing post-harvest infrastructure for agri-horti product exports, facilitation to exporters and creation of exports infrastructure at the borders. <br/><br/>(c)	No, Sir.<br/><br/>(d)	A suggestion was made to the participating State Governments that they may like to consider district level potentiality in their State export plans.<br/>(e)	The other steps taken by the Government to promote overall exports and push the country’s industrial growth are:<br/>	During the mid-term review of the Foreign Trade Policy in December, 2017, in order to boost exports, <br/>(i)	 incentives under Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS) were increased by 2% for labour intensive MSME sectors leading to additional annual incentive of Rs.4,567 Cr.<br/>(ii)	MEIS incentives were increased from 2% to 4% for Ready Made garments and Made ups in the labour intensive Textiles sector with an additional annual incentive of Rs.2,743 Cr.<br/>(iii)	Incentives under Services Exports From India Scheme (SEIS) have also been increased by 2% leading to additional annual incentive of Rs.1,140 Cr.<br/>Apart from the above, the Government is continuously taking steps to boost growth in industries which inter alia includes creating conducive business environment, strengthening infrastructure, strengthening intellectual property regimes, promoting investment and promoting the startup ecosystem.<br/>-----<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the spot market power prices and Indian Electricity Exchange prices have risen unexpectedly high in the last three years;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the reasons for the same;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether the production from wind and hydropower plants have gone down leading to decline in use of more renewable sources to produce electricity;<br/><br/>(d) 	if so, the reasons for the above decreased production; and<br/><br/>(e) 	how these increased prices are affecting the consumers and what measures are taken by Government to address the issue?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR POWER AND <br/>NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY<br/><br/>( SHRI  R.K. SINGH )<br/><br/>(a) & (b) : 	There are two power exchanges in India i.e. Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) and Power Exchange India Limited (PXIL), where electricity is being traded. The electricity prices are discovered on Day Ahead Market (DAM) of these power exchanges in every 15 minutes time block. These prices fluctuate in every time block, leading to fluctuations in a day, depending upon the electricity demand and supply position in the market at any given point in time.<br/><br/>The weighted average prices on DAM of these power exchanges during the last three years are as under:<br/>Year	Price on IEX (Rs/kWh)	Price on PXIL (Rs/kWh)<br/>2014-15	3.49	3.09<br/>2015-16	2.72	2.66<br/>2016-17	2.48	2.56<br/><br/>It can be seen from the above table that the average market clearing prices of electricity traded through power exchanges have decreased significantly over the last three years.<br/><br/>However, there were certain instances when spot market power prices have reached up to the level of Rs 9 to Rs 11 per kWh in some 15 minutes time block during some of the days during the month of September’17–November’17. Monthly average Market Clearing Prices (MCP) in the Indian power exchange during these months were Rs 4.09/Kwh (September’17), Rs. 4.08/Kwh (October’17) and Rs 3.55/ Kwh (November’17).<br/><br/>(c) & (d) : 	The production from wind and hydropower plants during the Financial Years (FY) 2014-15, 2015-16 and 2016-17 are given below:<br/><br/>	2014-15	2015-16	2016-17<br/>Wind ( In MU)	33768.30	33029.39	46004.34<br/>Hydro (in MU)	129244	121377	122378<br/>Total Renewable	61785	65781	81548<br/><br/>It can be observed from the above data that the wind and hydro generation had decreased during the FY 2015-16 but increased during the FY 2016-17. The overall generation from renewable sources have consistently increased during the FY 2015-16 and 2016-17.<br/>	<br/>(e) :		The share of electricity traded through power exchanges is only about 3% of the total electricity being consumed in the country. Hence the impact of any short term fluctuations, during 2 to 3 time blocks of 15 minutes each out of a total of 96 time blocks in a day, in electricity prices in the power exchange would have insignificant effect to the consumers. Through appropriate Regulations, Central Electricity Regulatory Commission ensures fair, neutral, efficient and robust functioning of power exchanges in India.<br/><br/>************* <br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) whether Government observed World Cancer Day, 2018 in the country; <br/><br/>(b) if so, details thereof along with the steps taken to achieve the aims and objectives of the event; <br/><br/>(c) the detailed programmes organised by Government to mark this occasion along with the funds allocated for this purpose; <br/><br/>(d) the details of various new treatments/innovations being introduced in the field of cancer globally during last three years; <br/><br/>(e) whether Government intends to adopt such new innovations, if so, details thereof and if not, reasons therefor; and   <br/><br/>(f) the other steps taken by Government to give assistance/facilities for research in treatment of cancer through Ayurveda?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a) to (c):     World Cancer day is observed on 4th February every year. Health is a state subject and the activities are carried out by State Governments for awareness of Cancer prevention and control. The details of activities carried out by State Governments is not maintained centrally. <br/><br/>The Indian Council of Medical Research’s –National Institute of Cancer Prevention and Research actively took  part in the ‘WALK FOR LIFE 2018’ on February 4th 2018 (World Cancer Day) at Rajpath, New Delhi. The public lecture on “Cancer Awareness”   was also given at All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi on February 4th 2018 so as to create awareness amongst public.<br/><br/>Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) under Ministry of AYUSH, through Central Ayurveda Research Institute for Cancer, Mumbai observed World Cancer Day by organizing Free Screening Camp for Breast, Cervix and Oral Cancer and Half Day Workshop on Cancer Awareness and Prevention” on 05.02.2018. The budgetary requirements were met from the Institute’s budget.<br/><br/>Union Government also used print and other forms of media such as Social Media to spread awareness. An amount of Rs. 67,80,600/- was released to Directorate of Advertising and Visual Publicity (DAVP) for the purpose, under National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS).<br/><br/>(d) & (e): There are various aspects of treatment modalities and prevention related to cancer. However, the data regarding new treatments/innovations in the field of cancer globally is not maintained centrally.<br/><br/>In the Government sector, research activities for detection and treatment of cancer are mostly carried out by Institutions/Departments such as the Indian Council of Medical Research, Department of Science and Technology and Department of Atomic Energy.  The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre has developed Bhabhatron and the Society for Applied Microwave Electronics Engineering and Research (SAMEER) has developed Linear Accelerator (LINAC).<br/><br/>Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) is promoting cancer research including epidemiological, clinical, basic and translational research.  ICMR has also developed protocols for the management (including treatment) of Buccal Mucosa Cancer, Gall Bladder Cancer, Stomach Cancer, Colorectal Cancer, and Tongue Cancer.  Institute of Cytology and Preventive Oncology under the Indian Council of Medical Research has developed a hand held device called Magnivisualizer with inbuilt source of light that can be used in field conditions for early detection of cervical cancer and oral cancer lesions.<br/><br/>(f):  The other steps taken by the Government are as under:-<br/><br/>(i)	The Ministry of AYUSH through Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy (CCRH) and Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM) have launched a programme to integrate Ayurveda, Homoeopathy and Unani with National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS) in one district each of six identified States. The major objective of the programme is prevention and early diagnosis of these diseases; reduce complications and drug dependency through these systems.<br/><br/>(ii)	CCRAS has developed a coded drug AYUSH QOL-2C for improving the quality of life in cancer patients. CCRAS has also undertaken research on coded drug Carctol-S under drug development. <br/><br/>(iii)	 A cross sectional study of cancer KAP (Knowledge, Attitude. and Practice) among Ayurveda and Allopathy fraternity has been started at Raja Ramdeo Anandilal Podar (RRAP) Central Ayurveda Research Institute for Cancer, Mumbai.<br/><br/>(iv)	Government has set up an All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA) at Sarita Vihar, New Delhi as an apex institute for Ayurveda, whose mandate includes research into treatment of cancer. AIIA has formed collaboration with National Institute for Cancer Prevention and Research (NICPR), Noida under Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) for conducting screening and spreading awareness for Breast and Cervical cancer, and with All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) for research in cancer prevention & treatment.<br/><br/>(v)	Under a collaboration with Tata Memorial Centre (TMC), Department of Atomic Energy, the Central Ayurvedic Research Institute in Cancer (CARIC), Mumbai, which is a unit of the CCRAS, undertakes integrative treatment procedures for the management of Cancer.<br/><br/>(vi) Government also supports intra-mural, extra-mural and collaborative research to encourage AYUSH Systems to develop procedures and therapies for management of cancer, through the units of its own Research Councils and Institutes, as well as through universities, hospitals and institutes.<br/>………<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.min_name: WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has observed Fifth India Water Week (IWW) recently, if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(b) the main theme of the event along with expenditure incurred for the said purpose; <br/><br/>(c) the number of Indian and foreign delegates who participated in the event along with achievement of the event; <br/><br/>(d) whether any such programme has been organised in the past in India; <br/><br/>(e) if so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(f) the other steps taken by Government for conservation, prevention and optimum utilisation of available water resources?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION & PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS<br/><br/>(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL)<br/><br/>(a & b) Yes, Sir.  MOWR,RD&GR organised 5th India Water Week-2017 during 10-14th   October, 2017 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The main theme of 5th India Water Week, 2017 was “Water and Energy for inclusive growth”. The total expenditure incurred for the event is Rs.2.32 Crore.<br/><br/>(c) About 1500 delegates representing National and International Organizations, Research Institutes, Educational Institutions and NGOs from water resources, agriculture, power sectors, etc., participated in the event that include 40 foreign delegates from 11  countries. Recommendations from the India Water Week have been circulated to concerned departments for implementation.<br/><br/>(d & e) MoWR,RD&GR has been organising India Water Week (IWW) since 2012.  So far, four India Water Week have been organised during the years 2012, 2013, 2015 & 2016  in New Delhi. The details are as below:<br/><br/>Sl no	Description	Period	Theme<br/>1.	1st IWW	10th-14th April 2012	Water, Energy and Food Security-Call for Solutions<br/>2.	2nd IWW	08th-12th April 2013	Efficient Water Management: Challenges and Opportunities<br/>3.	3rd IWW	13th-17th January 2015	Water Management for Sustainable Development<br/>4.	4th IWW	4th-8th April 2016	Water for all: Striving together<br/><br/><br/>(f) Water being a State subject, steps for augmentation, conservation and efficient management of water resources to ensure sustainability and availability are primarily undertaken by the respective State Governments. In order to supplement the efforts of the State Governments, the Central Government provides technical and financial assistance to State Governments through various schemes and programmes. The Central Government has taken various steps for conservation and optimum utilisation of water through various schemes like Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayi Yojana, Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme, Repair, Renovation & Restoration (RRR) of water bodies, implementation of new projects like Pancheshwar Dam, Polavaram Project, Interlinking of Rivers Project, Dam Rehabilitation & Improvement Project, etc. Additionally, non-structural measures have also been taken through the development and augmentation of National Hydrology Project, Flood Forecasting Stations, Hydrological Observation Stations, etc.<br/><br/>The other steps taken by Government for conservation, prevention and optimum utilisation of available water resources are:<br/><br/>•	With a view to improve water use efficiency in the irrigation projects of the country, the Government is promoting use of micro irrigation in the irrigated command.<br/><br/>•	The Government of India has also formulated a National Perspective Plan for Water Resources Development which envisages transfer of water from surplus basins to water deficit basins. The inter-basin transfer proposals envisage additional utilization of available water to bring additional area under irrigation<br/><br/>•	Under National Water Mission, 11 State Governments are being supported to formulate State Water Budgeting for Water Security, Safety and Sustainability as an innovative strategic intervention to check over-exploitation, water deficiency and contamination by building a convergence and synergy model aimed at performance based water governance.<br/><br/>•	Steps taken by the Central Government for conservation of water particularly ground water are available at the following URL http://mowr.gov.in/sites/default/files/MeasuresForGW-Depletion_1.pdf.<br/><br/>*****<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.min_name: WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION
records.qn_text: (a) whether a large quantity of water is lost through seepage from the unlined canals in the country; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; <br/><br/>(c) the estimated quantum of loss of water due to seepage from the unlined canals during the last three years; <br/><br/>(d) whether Government has taken up any steps to address the issue, if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(e) the amount made available and utilised for the purpose <br/>during the last three years scheme/programme-wise alongwith the achievement made thereunder; and <br/><br/>(f) the other steps taken by Government for prevention of seepage of water from canals?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION & PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c) The amount of water lost due to seepage from unlined canals varies widely with type of soil through which, the canal system passes and status of operation and maintenance of canals. As per “Guide for estimating irrigation water requirement, 1984 (Ministry of Irrigation)” seepage losses in lined canal are in range of 0.13 to 0.298 cumec per million square meter of wetted perimeter and that of unlined canal, from 0.9 to 3.05 cumec per million square meter of wetted perimeter.<br/><br/>(d) to (f) Water Resources Project are planned, funded, executed and maintained by the State Governments themselves as per their own resources and priority. In order to supplement the efforts of the State Governments, Ministry of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation provides technical and financial assistance to State Governments to encourage sustainable development and efficient management of water resources through various schemes and programmes such as Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) etc. under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sichayee Yojana (PMKSY). <br/>	 <br/>            PMKSY-AIBP do not provide specific funding for prevention of seepage from unlined canals. It provides funding for completion of ongoing irrigation projects and extension, renovation and modernization (ERM) projects. Further, in the ERM projects several measures are taken including lining of vulnerable reaches to improve efficiency of water use.<br/>	<br/>		During 2016-17, ninety nine (99) ongoing Major/Medium irrigation projects under AIBP, having potential of 76.03 lakh ha. have been prioritized in consultation with States, for completion in phases up to December, 2019 along with their Command Area Development & Water Management (CADWM) works. Funding mechanism through NABARD has been approved by the Government for both central and state share.<br/><br/>	     Out of these 99 projects, 10 projects have been categorized as ERM. Central assistance (CA) of Rs. 90.93 cr. and Rs. 217.96 cr. has been released for these 10 ERM projects during 2016-17 and 2017-18 (so far) respectively. <br/>*****<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether there have been any cases where differently-abled persons have been denied Aadhaar card; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(c) the steps taken to provide Aadhaar cards to people with neurological disabilities who are not able to sit still for the photograph or the iris scan; <br/><br/>(d) whether all Aadhaar centres have disabled friendly access infrastructure; and <br/><br/>(e) the steps taken to ensure that Aadhaar card registration process is made viable for differently-abled persons?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) and (b): No, Sir. Every resident, including differently-abled persons, is eligible for Aadhaar.<br/><br/>(c), (d) and (e): Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) has laid down well defined processes for Aadhaar enrolment of those persons who are not able to provide some or any of their biometrics, due to any reasons, including disability, while enrolling for Aadhaar.<br/><br/>As per requirement, special measures are taken for Aadhaar enrolment of specific groups, including holding special enrolment camps etc. In deserving cases, household visits are also organised.<br/><br/>Aadhaar centres are run by Registrars/ Enrolment Agencies who are required to ensure various guidelines including facilitation of residents at enrolment centres. Enrolment operations are now being shifted to post offices and branch premises of scheduled commercial banks. The Department of Posts and banks can ensure convenience of the disabled persons while providing services to them, as per their policies in this regard.<br/><br/>******<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Loan scheme under Rashtriya Mahila Kosh
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	the details of the loan schemes operating under Rashtriya Mahila Kosh (RMK) during the last three years and the current year; State/UT-wise;<br/><br/>(b)	whether it is a fact that no loans were issued under RMK during the financial year 2015-16, if so, whether the lending resumed;<br/><br/>(c)	if not, what measures have been taken to address the issue; and<br/><br/>(d)	whether the annual reports for RMK scheme are available for the latest years on the scheme website, if not, what measures have been taken to address the issue?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT <br/>(DR. VIRENDRA KUMAR)<br/><br/>(a)	Rashtriya Mahila Kosh (RMK), a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (MWCD), and an apex micro-finance organization provides micro-credit at concessional rate of interest to women Self Help Groups or individual women (the ultimate beneficiaries) through Intermediary Micro-financing Organizations (IMOs) /Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs)/ Voluntary Organisations (VOs) for various livelihood support and income generating activities. <br/><br/>The details of loan schemes being implemented for empowerment of women through Non-Government Organisations by the Rashtriya Mahila Kosh (RMK) across the country are given at Annexure-I and the the details of Loan sanctioned and disbursed by RMK during last three years and the current year, State/ UT-wise are given at Annexure-II.<br/><br/>(b)	&(c) Yes Sir. The Lending Guidelines of RMK were under revision during the financial year 2015-16, hence no loans were issued by RMK. The revised Lending Guidelines of RMK has been approved for implementation and the lending activity has also been resumed.<br/><br/>(c)	Annual Reports of RMK till the financial year 2015-16 are ready and available for uploading on the RMK website. RMK website is under reconstruction to address the issue.<br/><br/>*******<br/><br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether the National Council of Education Research and Training (NCERT) has conducted National Achievement Survey, 2017; <br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and aims and objective behind the move; <br/>(c) the number of students who had been covered under the survey; <br/>(d) whether NCERT had conducted similar survey earlier also; <br/>(e) if so, the outcome of the said survey; and <br/>(f) the other steps taken by Government to check the gaps in learning in Government and Government aided schools?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI UPENDRA KUSHWAHA)<br/><br/>(a)	to (c): Yes, Sir. National Achievement Survey (NAS) 2017 was conducted by the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) on             13th November, 2017. The learning levels of around 22 lakh students of Classes III, V and VIII from nearly 1.10 lakh schools across 700 districts in all 36 States and UTs were assessed. Students of Classes III and V were assessed on Reading Comprehension, Mathematics and Environmental Studies and Class VIII students were assessed on Language, Maths, Science and Social Science. This competency based assessment was based on the Learning Outcomes developed by NCERT. Along with the test items, questionnaires pertaining to students, teachers and schools were also used. Based on the NAS results, the teachers can understand exactly the learning needs of students at different levels, required pedagogies for teachings, and how to measure and ensure that children have reached the required level.<br/><br/>(d) to (e): NCERT has conducted periodic national surveys of learning achievement of children in classes III, V and VIII. Four rounds of National Achievement Survey (NAS) for class V and three rounds for classes III & VIII have been conducted earlier. These surveys reveal improvement in learning achievement levels of pupils, in identified subjects from first round to fourth round. Similarly, NCERT has also conducted the NAS at class X. However, only first round of NAS has been conducted at class X level.<br/>A web based application has been developed for generating the district wise learning report cards for NAS to reflect the disaggregated and detailed learning levels and to identify the gaps in learning outcomes at district level. <br/>(f): In order to focus on quality education, the Central Rules to the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) have been amended on 20th February, 2017 to include reference on class-wise, subject-wise Learning Outcomes. Learning outcomes are assessment standards indicating the expected levels of learning that children should achieve for that class. These indicators can be used as check points to assess learning at different points of time. The Learning Outcomes for each class at elementary stage in Languages (Hindi, English and Urdu), Mathematics, Environmental Studies, Science and Social Science have been finalized and shared with all States and UTs. <br/>The Central Government through the Centrally Sponsored Schemes of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) and Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA) supports States/UTs to improve quality of education at elementary and secondary level, respectively. Under these schemes, the State Governments and UT Administrations are supported on several interventions to improve quality of education, teaching standards, including regular in-service teachers’ training, induction training for newly recruited teachers, recruitment of additional teachers for improving pupil teacher ratio, academic support for teachers through block and cluster resource centres, Maths and Science kits, Lab equipment, special teaching for learning enhancement, ICT facilities in schools, introduction of vocational education component at the secondary level, infrastructural strengthening of schools, etc.<br/>*****

records.qtitle: Approval of two new skill development schemes
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has approved two new skill development schemes recently;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof along with the aims and objectives for starting these two schemes;<br/><br/>(c)	the amount earmarked for these schemes; and<br/><br/>(d)	the time by when these two schemes will be made operational?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) to (d)	The Government of India has approved two new World Bank loan assisted projects known as Skill Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion (SANKALP) and Skills Strengthening for Industrial Value Enhancement (STRIVE). Both the schemes are aimed at institutional reform and quality improvement in skill development and Vocational Education and Training (VET).<br/><br/>SANKALP is an outcome based centrally sponsored scheme which aimed at strengthening institutes, improving quality and access, and catalyzing private sector investments in Short-term Skill Development. The project is worth Rs. 4475 Crore is to be implemented over six years.<br/><br/>STRIVE is a central sector scheme which envisaged to improve relevance and efficiency of skills development provided through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and apprenticeship. The scheme aims at integrating and enhancing delivery quality of 500 ITIs including 100 Private ITIs. The total cost of STRIVE scheme is Rs. 2200 crore. The financing agreement between the Government of India and the World Bank has been signed on 19th December 2017 and scheme duration is 5 years from year 2017-2022.<br/>

records.qtitle: Revival of Gas based power plants
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government is aware that several gas based power plants have been stranded;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof along with the action taken thereon;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether any subsidies and tax concessions are being offered to those plants and if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(d) 	whether Government is now planning to revive 25GW stranded gas based capacity to push consumption of the fuel and transform the nation into a gas based economy; and<br/><br/>(e) 	the time by when a decision in the matter will be taken?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR POWER AND <br/>NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY <br/><br/>(SHRI  R.K. SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) :	A total of 14305 MW gas based power generation capacity is stranded in the country due to non-availability of domestic gas. Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoP&NG) have informed that  domestic gas is being supplied to the power sector as per current production level and domestic natural gas supply to power sector can improve only in case production levels increase in future and as per prevailing MoP&NG guidelines. <br/><br/>(c) to (e) :    	Government has provided for Nil Customs duty on import of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) and Natural Gas (NG), if it is used for generation of electrical energy by a generating company, as defined in section 2(28) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (36 of 2003) to supply electrical energy or to engage in the business of supplying electrical energy to the grid. The Gas based power plants are free to import the LNG, generate power and sell it to the consumers. <br/><br/>					 ***********<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of AYURVEDA, YOGA & NATUROPATHY, UNANI, SIDDHA AND HOMOEOPATHY be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) whether Government observed 2nd Ayurveda Day on 17th October, 2017; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(c) the main theme of the Ayurveda Day; <br/><br/>(d) the number of delegates that participated in the event; <br/><br/>(e) the issues discussed on the occasion of 2nd Ayurveda Day and the outcome therefor; and <br/><br/>(f) the other steps taken by Government for promotion of Ayurveda in the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYURVEDA,<br/>YOGA & NATUROPATHY, UNANI, SIDDHA AND HOMOEOPATHY<br/>(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK)<br/>(a):      Yes.<br/><br/>(b) to (e):      2nd Ayurveda Day was celebrated on 16th & 17th October, 2017 with the theme of “Ayurveda for Pain Management”. On 16th October, 2017, One day National Seminar on “Ayurveda for Pain Management” and “AYUSH–CII Industry Conclave” in which the central theme was developing strategies to facilitate the growth of Ayurveda’s market size were held at  India Habitat Centre, New Delhi. Approximately 500 delegates participated in the Seminar. The main function of Ayurveda Day was celebrated at All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), Sarita Vihar on 17th October, 2017 and AIIA was dedicated to the nation. Approximately 1500 delegates participated in the event. <br/>Contd……..<br/>-2-<br/> 	 Aspects related to Pain Management through Ayurveda and how to promote Ayurveda Market in coming years were discussed. The Ministry developed the “Ayurvedic Standard Treatment Guidelines” which were released on this occasion.  A short film on scientific relevance of Ayurveda was screened and National AYUSH Morbidity & Standardized Terminologies Portal (NAMSTP) was also launched on this occasion.<br/>(f):      Ministry of AYUSH, Govt. of India has setup Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences for undertaking coordinating formulating, developing and promoting research on scientific lines in Ayurvedic sciences through medicinal plant research (Medico-ethno botanical survey, pharmacognosy and tissue culture), Drug Standardization Pharmacological Research, Clinical Research Literary Research and Documentation. The activities of the Council are carried out through 30 institutes/ Centres/ Units located all over India and also through collaborative studies with various universities, hospitals and institutes. <br/><br/>           The Ministry of AYUSH has been implementing AYUSH intervention in NPCDCS for prevention and control of Non Communicable diseases in 01 district each of 06 states viz Surendra Nagar (Gujarat), Bhilwara (Rajasthan), Gaya (Bihar), Lakhimpur Kheri (Uttar Pradesh.), Krishna District (Andhra Pradesh.) & Darjeeling (West Bengal), Ayurveda intervention is being implemented in three districts, Unani in 01 district and Homeopathy in 02 districts. Ministry of AYUSH launched Mission Madhumeha on the 1st Ayurveda day which was celebrated on 28.10.2016. The Ministry also developed protocol for prevention and control of Diabetes through Ayurveda and it was released on the occasion of the 1st Ayurveda Day.<br/><br/>          Under the IEC Scheme, the Ministry takes up initiatives for propagation and promotion of AYUSH systems of medicine including Ayurveda by organizing Arogya Fairs/Melas, Ayurveda Parv, Conferences, Exhibitions, Seminars, Workshops, Symposium and also undertakes publicity through electronic multimedia, print media campaigning for awareness amongst the citizens all over the country. <br/>…………<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether a large number of fake or duplicate driving licences are under circulation and if so, whether Government has taken any steps to check the menace; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(c) whether Government is planning to link all 1,300 RTOs to the central depository; <br/><br/>(d) if so, whether this issue was taken up at the Transport Development Council meeting; <br/><br/>(e) if so, the outcome thereof; and <br/><br/>(f) the other steps taken by Government to check the menace of multiple licencing?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI MANSUKH L. MANDAVIYA)<br/><br/>(a) to (f)  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways does not maintain centralised data regarding fake or duplicate driving licences. However, as per an analysis done in January, 2015 on National Register for Driving Licences by National Informatics Centre (NIC), it was found that there is a possibility of duplicate licences. As on 5th January, 2015, out of total 6,70,16,851 driving licences records available,  16,72,138 records were found to be possible duplicates spread over 7,99,923 clusters.  The percentage of probable duplicates stands at 2.5 percent as per this exercise. This information has been shared with respective states for further action. 	<br/><br/>National Database on Driving Licenses and Vehicle registration has already been created. National Informatics Centre (NIC) who has been entrusted with the design, development, computerization roll-out and maintenance of the VAHAN and SARATHI project across all the states and Union Territory Administrations has achieved almost 100% success in terms of deployment of core Schema/product for Vehicle Registration (VAHAN) and for Driving Licenses (SARATHI) across the country. Subsequently to consolidate the database, State Register (SR) for all the states and National Register (NR) were established. Almost all the sites in 36 States/Union Territory Administrations are connected. More than 20 crore Vehicle records and 10 crore Driving License records are available in National Register repository. State Transport Departments and enforcement agencies have been provided access to data on National Register to facilitate instant verification of all driving licenses (DLs)/ Registration Certificate (RCs) and the digitalized data is also made accessible through Mobile by sending SMS from their registered number.<br/>	<br/>The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Bill, 2017, passed by Lok Sabha and presently in Rajya Sabha for consideration and passing, provides for centralised register of driving licences. This will further help to carry reforms in the driving licence testing process and eliminating the duplicate licences.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether the Government has decided to conduct an independent audit of all 50,000 odd Aadhaar enrolment centres and inspect them in person; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and the aims and objectives behind the move;<br/><br/>(c) by when audit of Aadhaar centres will commence and be completed; <br/><br/>(d) whether UIDAI is launching a major information drive to impress upon people the benefits of linking their Aadhaar with their bank account, PAN, mobile number; and<br/><br/>(e)  if so, the response of the people thereto?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: (a), (b) and (c): In accordance with Regulation 21(6), 23(6) and 26(2) of Aadhaar Enrolment and Update) Regulations, 2016, Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) conducts audit and inspection of the enrolment centres through requisite number of personnel.<br/><br/>(d) and (e): UIDAI through print, electronic and social media regularly makes the people aware on various aspects of Aadhaar, including benefits of linking their Aadhaar with their bank accounts, Permanent Account Numbers and mobile numbers. As on 8th December 2017, around 71.24 crore mobile numbers, 14.63 crore Permanent Account Numbers and 82 crore bank accounts have been linked with Aadhaar. <br/><br/>******<br/><br/> <br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a)	the details of funds allocated for the scheme of Shelter for Urban Homeless (SUH) under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Urban Livelihoods Mission during the last three years, State-wise and year-wise;<br/>(b)	the number of shelters constructed and operational and shelters under construction in the country, State-wise and city-wise;<br/>(c)	the percentage of sanctioned shelters in the country that have been completed and are operational and whether the Ministry finds this percentage satisfactory; and<br/>(d)	the number of shelters for every 1,00,000 people in Lucknow, Varanasi, Delhi, Mumbai and Kanpur?<br/> <br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF <br/>THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN AFFAIRS<br/>               [SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI]<br/> <br/><br/>(a)	: Under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM) funds are allocated to States in a consolidated manner out of which appropriate amount is apportioned by States/UTs for Scheme of Shelter for Urban Homeless (SUH), as per their requirements.  Under the scheme, a total of Rs. 120157.14 Lakhs have been released to States/UTs during the last three years.  A statement showing Year-wise and State-wise release of funds under DAY-NULM is at Annexure-I.<br/><br/>(b) & (c): As per information available, as on 30.11.2017, a total of 1331 shelters have been sanctioned by 25 States/UTs. Out of this, 789 shelters have become operational and remaining are under different stages of construction/ refurbishment. A statement showing the State/UT-wise shelters sanctioned and operational under SUH is at Annexure II.  It would be noted that about sixty percent of the total shelters sanctioned have become operational under the DAY-NULM. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs constantly pursues with States/ UTs to reduce the gap between number of shelters sanctioned and made operational. <br/><br/>(d): Under the DAY-NULM, there is a provision for construction of permanent shelters for a minimum of one hundred persons for every 1,00,000 urban population. As per the information received from the referred States, there are 23 shelters in Lucknow (out of which 02 are under the DAY-NULM), 14 shelters in Varanasi (all Non-NULM), 30 shelters in Kanpur (out of which 03 are under the DAY-NULM) and 32 shelters in Mumbai (out of which 09 are under the DAY-NULM). In Delhi there are 83 pucca, 113 porta cabin and 57 temporary shelter in tents (for winter seasons only). Out of total shelters in Delhi, 201shelters are under the DAY-NULM.<br/>

records.qtitle: Achievement in World Food India 2017 event
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	Whether Government organized a mega global food event – World Food India from 3rd to 5th November, 2017 in Delhi, if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(b)	the number of Indian and foreign delegates that participated in the event along with the achievements made in the event;<br/><br/>(c)	whether any programme of such kind had been organized in the country in the past, if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(d)	the other steps taken by Government to create environment for bringing higher returns for farmers, creating employment and fostering entrepreneurship ?  <br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>(a) to (c):  Ministry of Food Processing Industries had organized “ World Food India 2017” during 3-5 Nov 2017 in New Delhi for the first time. The event attracted great support and participation of 61 countries, 27 States of India and 60 global CEOs among others. There were closed to 800 global and domestic exhibitors and around 75000 business visitors.  Investment intent of about USD 13.56 billion were received during the event.<br/><br/><br/> (d):   The other steps include the recently launched Central Sector Scheme PRADHAN MANTRI KISAN SAMPADA YOJANA (PMKSY) by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries. PMKSY is an umbrella scheme for overall development of the food processing sector. PMKSY encompasses three new schemes viz; (i) Infrastructure for Agro-Processing Clusters; (ii) Creation of Backward and Forward Linkages and (iii) Creation / Expansion of Food Processing & Preservation Capacities and four on-going schemes viz; (i) Mega Food Parks; (ii) Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure; (iii) Food Safety and Quality Assurance Infrastructure; and (iv) Human Resources and Institutions. <br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether Government''s attention is drawn towards recent complaints regarding private vendors on alleged leakage of UID data, if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government has approved setting up of Aadhaar centres in post offices, if so, the details thereof and the objective behind the move;<br/><br/>(c) the amount allocated for setting up Aadhaar centres in post offices;<br/><br/>(d) the estimated number of post offices where this facility will be available; and<br/><br/>(e) by when Aadhaar centres in post offices will start functioning?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>a): There has been no leakage of Aadhaar data from UIDAI Central Identities Data Repository (CIDR).<br/><br/>(b): Considering its wide scale presence across the country, Department of Post, as Registrar of UIDAI, has been mandated to set up Aadhaar enrolment and update facility in designated post offices throughout the country.<br/><br/>(c): UIDAI has till date released Rs.8 crore to Department of Post under ICT Assistance. In addition, Rs.200 crore has been allocated by the Government for setting up Aadhaar Enrolment & Update Centres.<br/><br/>(d) and (e): Department of Post is expected to set up about 13,500 Aadhaar enrolment/update centres in designated post offices progressively by the financial year 2017-18. <br/><br/>********<br/><br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has any data about the number of drug abuse cases reported across the country during the last three years; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(c) whether Government has requested all the States to identify vulnerable districts which report high number of drug abuse cases and are underserved by the current healthcare system; <br/><br/>(d) if so, the details thereof and the response of the State Government thereto; and <br/><br/>(e) the other steps taken by Government to propose a national policy to fight drug addiction?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT<br/>(SHRI VIJAY SAMPLA)<br/>(a) & (b): The last National Survey on the extent, pattern and trend of drug abuse was sponsored by Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and conducted by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime in the year 2000-2001. The report was published in 2004.  The Survey estimated that about 7.32 Crore persons in India were users of alcohol and drugs. Of these 87 lakh used Cannabis, 20 lakh used opiates and 6.25 Crore were users of Alcohol. The survey covered 40,697 individuals. Only males within the age group of 12-60 years were part of the Survey. <br/>	The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is now undertaking a National level Survey in collaboration with National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre, AIIMS, New Delhi. A Memorandum of Understanding was signed in August, 2016. The survey will provide national and state-level estimates of proportion and absolute number of individuals using various drugs and suffering from substance use disorders. <br/><br/>(c) & (d): The Ministry has issued an Advisory on 11.08.2016 to all the States/UTs on combating drug abuse which, inter-alia, includes  preparation of action plan by all States/UTs for ensuring facility of de-addiction centres in each district or as per prevalence of addiction, ensuring adequate facilities in every government hospital in next five years with priority to severely affected/underserved regions and districts, assessing the need and ensuring increase in the number of Integrated Rehabilitation Centres for Addicts (IRCAs) and Regional Resource & Training Centres (RRTCs), establishing separate and specialized de-addiction treatment centres/facilities for drug dependent females, ensuring availability of treatment for those in Juvenile Homes, Children Homes and Prisons, adopting approaches for education and prevention at all levels including schools and colleges etc. So far, this Ministry has received action plans from Nineteen State Governments/Union Territory Administrations.<br/><br/><br/>(e): The Ministry has already formulated a draft National Policy on Drug Demand Reduction and the same is being finalized.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: India s ranking in Global Hunger Index
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a)	the details of India’s ranking in the Global Hunger Index report during the last three years;<br/><br/>(b)	whether a substantial proportion of the population continue to suffer from lack of food according to the said report;<br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof and measures taken in this regard; and <br/><br/>(d)	whether the Country’s Global Hunger Index score is lower as compared to those of developing countries and if so the details thereof and the reasons therefor? <br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS<br/><br/>        (RAO INDERJIT SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) to (d)  The International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) has been bringing out the Reports on Global Hunger Index (GHI) every year since 2006.  The latest Report on GHI for the year 2017 ranks India at 100th out of 119 countries compared to 97th amongst 118 countries in the year 2016 and 80th out of 104 countries in the year 2015.  However, this does not signify worsening food situation in India.  In fact, the GHI 2017 report acknowledges that India’s GHI score has consistently improved from 46.2 in 1992 to 38.2 in 2000 and further to 35.6 in 2008 and 31.4 in 2017. It is better than some of the developing countries like Pakistan, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe, etc.  <br/><br/>	The Government of India accords high priority to the issue of hunger and malnutrition and is implementing several schemes/ programmes to improve food security situation in the country.  Government allocates foodgrains at highly subsidized prices to States and Union Territories under National Food Security Act 2013 covering upto 75% population in rural areas and 50% population in urban areas. Government is also implementing other welfare schemes like Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), National Health Mission (NHM), Mid-day Meal (MDM) Scheme, Integrated Child Development Services Scheme (ICDS), Annapurna Scheme for the senior citizens, Nutritional Programme for Adolescent Girls, Emergency Feeding Programme, etc.   Besides, Government of India has recently approved setting up of National Nutrition Mission to ensure holistic development and adequate nutrition for pregnant women, mothers and children. The programme targets to reduce the level of stunting, under-nutrition, anaemia and low birth weight amongst babies.<br/><br/>                     ------<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether the Ministry has cancelled the licence of 4842 NGOs and organisations under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA); <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; <br/><br/>(c) whether earlier also many NGOs failed to adhere to FCRA norms; <br/><br/>(d) if so, the action taken by Government therefor; and <br/><br/>(e) if so, the details thereof along with  the list of NGOs which got permission from the Ministry during the last two years?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	Yes Sir. In the year 2017, since 4842 NGOs did not submit annual returns in compliance with FCRA, 2010 and Rules made there under, their registrations were cancelled.  The details of cancellation of registration certificate are available on the FCRA web Portal www.fcraonline.nic.in of the Ministry of Home affairs. <br/><br/>(c), (d) & (e):	As per available information, in the year 2015, registration of more than 8500 NGOs were cancelled for not adhering to the provisions of FCRA 2010 and Rules made thereunder.<br/><br/><br/><br/>                           ******

records.qtitle: Increasing the strength of Rapid Action Force
records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has decided to increase the strength of Rapid Action Force by adding five new battalions; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and the objective behind the move; <br/><br/>(c) whether Rapid Action Force battalions of CRPF have been located in several States; <br/><br/>(d) if so, the number of States that have submitted proposal for establishment of a Ripid Action Force battalion of CRPF in the State; and <br/><br/>(e) if so, the details thereof and the time by which such battalion is likely to be established in Rajasthan?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a) to (b):	Considering the increased demand of various State Governments for Central Forces to assist them in controlling riot and riot-like situations, Government vide order dated 21.9.2016 has approved raising 5 more Rapid Action Force (RAF) Battalions by converting 5 existing General Duty battalions of CRPF.<br/>(c):	The existing RAF Battalions are located in Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telengana, Tamil Nadu and Delhi. <br/>…2/<br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/>R.S.US.Q.NO.565 FOR 20.12.2017<br/><br/>(d) to (e):	Since 2013, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana, Karnataka, Rajasthan and Tripura have requested for establishment of RAF in their States.  The Key Location Plan of the new five RAF Bns are in the States of Haryana, Karnataka, Bihar, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.  Sanction for manpower for the five new RAF Bns have since been accorded. In respect of Rajasthan, sanction has also been issued for acquisition of 50 acres land at Jaipur (Rajasthan).<br/><br/><br/><br/>                            ******

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has identified stressed power projects of various public and private sector companies in the country;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof, as on date, along with the amount stuck in these projects, as on date, State/UT-wise, company-wise;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether Government is formulating a novel scheme to revive stressed power assets by inviting competitive bids from them to supply electricity for five years, if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(d) 	the steps taken or being taken by Government to expedite completion of such stressed power projects?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR POWER AND <br/>NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY <br/><br/>(SHRI  R.K. SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) :	Generation of Electricity is a de-licensed activity and promoters put up project based on their own assessment.  However, Government has reviewed the status of 34 coal based stressed Power Projects, as per the list provided by Department of Financial Services. The details of such stressed projects along with the amount stuck in these projects as per information available, as on date, State/UT-wise, company-wise are Annexed.<br/><br/>(c) :	The Government is constantly evaluating the stress in the Power sector and taking required measures in consultation with other stakeholders to encourage procurement of Power. In this regard, Power Finance Corporation has been designated as the nodal agency to ascertain and aggregate the power requirement of the States. <br/><br/>(d) :	The Government has also taken a number of steps for completion of stressed/stalled projects which include setting up of Project Monitoring Group (PMG) under Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) to track stalled projects, both in the public and private sectors and to remove implementation bottlenecks in these projects on a fast-track basis. Central Electricity Authority (CEA) monitors the progress of under construction power projects through frequent site visits and interaction with the developers, equipment suppliers and other stakeholders to identify issues critical for commissioning of projects and help in resolving them.  Regular reviews are also undertaken by Ministry of Power, Ministry of Heavy Industries and Cabinet Secretariat to identify the constraint areas and facilitate quick resolution of inter-ministerial and other outstanding issues. A Power Project Monitoring Panel (PPMP) has been set up by the Ministry of Power for monitoring of on-going Thermal and Hydro Generation projects along with the associated transmission system. Stalled Projects are also discussed in PRAGATI meetings at the highest level to resolve the bottlenecks in implementation of projects, as and when required.<br/>**********<br/>

records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/><br/>(a) Details of NPAs of public and private sector banks, and reduction in their NPAs due to recoveries in percentage terms, are at Annexure.<br/>(b) and (c): Vigilance side has apprised that no complaint from union of bank employees to investigate into the top 100 NPA accountholders has been dealt with by it.<br/>(d): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has introduced Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets (S4A), Strategic Debt Restructuring Scheme (SDR), Flexible Structuring (5/25) schemes for restructuring debt, issued guidelines on Joint Lenders’ Forum (JLF) for resolution, and issued Corrective Action Plan (CAP) for rectification, recovery and restructuring processes, to address stress because of NPAs.<br/>**********<br/><br/><br/> <br/>  Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No. 391, for 19.12.2017<br/><br/>Annexure<br/><br/>Percentage of Gross Non-performing Assets (NPAs) to Gross Advances of Public and Private Sector Banks<br/><br/>	2014-15	2015-16	2016-17	2017-18 (till September 2017)<br/>Public Sector Banks	4.97%	9.27%	11.66%	12.59%<br/>Private Sector Banks	2.10%	2.83%	  4.05%	 4.20%<br/>Source: RBI (Global Operations)<br/><br/><br/><br/>Data on reduction in NPAs due to actual recoveries as percentage of Gross NPA for Public and Private Sector Banks<br/><br/>	2014-15	2015-16	2016-17	2017-18 (till September 2017)<br/>Public Sector Banks	15.19%	7.58%	7.78%	3.99%<br/>Private Sector Banks	17.63%	15.02%	16.62%	9.94%<br/>Source: RBI (Global Operations)<br/><br/>*********<br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.min_name: WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government is aware that 196 dams in the country are more than 100 years old and if so, the details thereof; <br/>(b) whether Government is planning to conduct a break analysis of 5247 large dams across the country and put in place an emergency action plan especially for the 196 dams that are over 100 years old; and <br/>(c) if so, the details thereof and the time by which the proposed examination of dams will be started and completed?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION, ROAD TRANSPORT & HIGHWAYS AND SHIPPING <br/><br/>(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)<br/><br/>(a) to (c)   A statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/> <br/><br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED IN REPLY TO PARAS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.  *28 TO BE ANSWERED ON 18th DECEMBER, 2017 ON “ACTION PLAN FOR OLD DAMS” RAISED BY SHRI SANJAY SETH<br/><br/>(a)  Yes, Sir. As per National Register of Large Dams, 195 Dams are more than 100 years old. The State-wise details are at Annexure-I.<br/><br/>(b) & (c) Water Resource being a State subject, the upkeep and safety of Dams including Dam Break Analysis (DBA) and Emergency Action Plan (EAP) rests primarily with dam owners which are State Governments, central and State power generating PSUs, Municipalities and private companies etc. However a Committee headed by Chairman, Central Water Commission (CWC) named National Committee on Dam Safety (NCDS) comprising of representatives from State Water Resource Departments (WRD) and PSUs has been formed by MoWR, RD & GR. In the meetings of NCDS, the State Governments/Dam owners were requested to prepare the Emergency Action Plan (which includes DBA) of each large dam as per guidelines of CWC. As per information provided by various State Governments, 363 EAPs have been prepared as per details placed at Annexure-II.<br/><br/>Moreover, Govt. of India has taken up the Dam Rehabilitation and Improvement Project (DRIP) with loan assistance from World Bank for rehabilitation and improvement of about 250 dams initially in seven States (Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, and Uttarakhand) and for institutional strengthening and project management in Central Water Commission (CWC) and Implementing Agencies. <br/><br/> 	Under DRIP, an EAP has been prepared for Hirakud Dam as a Model EAP for circulation to all the dam owners in the country for replication for the dams under their jurisdiction. So far under the project, Dam Break Analysis and Inundation Maps (essential input for preparing an EAP) of 105 DRIP dams have been prepared out of which one is more than 100 years old. For the dams which are not covered in the DRIP, State Govts/Dam owners have been requested to carry out the DBA and prepare EAPs. DBA for the Mulla Periyar dam which is also more than 100 years old, has been carried out. The list of dams for which dam break analysis and inundation maps have been prepared under DRIP is given at Annexure-III. <br/><br/> 	A guideline on “Developing Emergency Action Plan for Dams” has also been prepared and circulated to the States and dam owners for adoption. <br/>*****<br/><br/><br/>ANNEXURE -I<br/><br/>Annexure referred in reply to para (a) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 28 to be answered on 18.12.2017.<br/>S.No.	Name of the Dam	Year of Completion 	River	Seismic zone	Type of Dam	Length of dam (m)	Gross Storage  capacity<br/>(103 M3)	Reservoir  Area (103 M2)	Effective Storage Capacity  (103 M3)<br/>ANDHRA PRADESH<br/>1. records.qn_text: (a) 	whether India has entered into Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and Nepal Motor Vehicle Agreement (BBIN MVA); <br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(c) 	whether Bhutan has backed out and more recently Bangladesh is also expressing its reluctance to BBIN MVA;<br/> <br/>(d) 	if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(e) 	whether India has made a fresh pitch to fast track the BBIN MVA?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI MANSUKH L. MANDAVIYA)<br/><br/>(a) & (b): Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and Nepal (BBIN) signed a framework Motor Vehicle Agreement (MVA) in June 2015 to enable movement of passenger and cargo vehicles across borders among the four countries.  <br/><br/>(c) to (e): Bhutan, being one of the signatories to the BBIN MVA, has not yet ratified the Agreement for its entry into force.  Pending ratification, however, Bhutan has given its consent for the BBIN MVA to enter into force amongst the other 3 countries i.e. Bangladesh, India and Nepal, who have already ratified it. India has, therefore, approached Bangladesh and Nepal through diplomatic channels for evolving modalities to operationalise the MVA among Bangladesh, India and Nepal (BIN).   <br/><br/>* * * * * <br/>

records.name: Sanjay Seth
records.qn_text: (a) whether big cities of the country have reported big rise in road accidents in 2016 as compared to the previous year;<br/> <br/>(b) if so, the number of road accidents and the number of people who died in such accidents during the last two years, National Highway-wise and State-wise; <br/><br/>(c) whether Government has assessed the major reasons for road accidents, if so, the details thereof and the action taken in this regard; and<br/><br/> (d) the other steps taken by Government to prevent the road accidents and spread awareness in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI MANSUKH L. MANDAVIYA)<br/><br/>(a) 	The total number of accidents in million plus cities for the calendar year 2015 and 2016 are 1,11,024 and 89,835 respectively. The total number of road accidents in million plus has decreased in 2016 in comparison to 2015.<br/><br/>(b) 	The total no. of road accidents and persons killed in road accidents on National Highways including Expressways, State –wise, for the last two years i.e. calendar year 2015 and 2016 is annexed.<br/><br/>(c) &(d) Any road accident is multi-causal. Ideally, the factor responsible should be established through objective assessment of the circumstances under which the road accident occurred. Based on the extant data reporting system, drivers’ fault was single most important factor responsible for 84% of  road accidents on all roads in the country in 2016. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has taken a number of steps to prevent such road accidents as per details mentioned under:<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>i.	Setting up of model driving training institutes in States and refresher training to drivers of Heavy Motor Vehicle in the unorganized sector.<br/>ii.	Advocacy/Publicity campaign on road safety through the electronic and print media. <br/>iii.	Tightening of safety standards for vehicles like Seat Belts, anti-lock braking system etc.<br/>iv.	The Government has approved a National Road Safety Policy.  This Policy outlines various policy measures such as promoting awareness, establishing road safety information data base, encouraging safer road infrastructure including application of intelligent transport, enforcement of safety laws etc.<br/>v.	The Government has constituted the National Road Safety Council as the apex body to take policy decisions in matters of road safety.  <br/>vi.	The Ministry has requested all States/UTs for setting up of State Road Safety Council and District Road Safety Committees, and to hold their meetings regularly.<br/>vii.	The Ministry has constituted Group of Ministers of State Transport Minister to examine the best practices of Transport and suggest issues to improve road safety. <br/>viii.	Based on the recommendation of Group of Minister, the Ministry introduced Motor Vehicle (Amendment) Bill 2017 covering entire gamut of road safety. <br/>ix.	The Ministry has formulated a multi-pronged strategy to address the issue of road safety based on 4 ‘E’s viz. Education, Engineering (both of roads and vehicles), Enforcement and Emergency Care. <br/>x.	Road safety has been made an integral part of road design at planning stage.  <br/>xi.	Road Safety Audit of selected stretches of National Highways has been taken up.<br/>xii.	High priority has been accorded to identification and rectification of black spots (accident prone spots) on national highways. <br/>xiii.	The threshold for four laning of national highway has been reduced from 15,000 Passenger Car Units (PCUs) to 10,000 PCUs. About 52,000 Km of stretches of State Highways has been identified for conversion to national highways.<br/><br/>****<br/><br/> <br/><br/>Annexure <br/>ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (b) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 255 ANSWERED ON  18/12/.2017 ASKED BY SHRI SANJAY SETH,  <br/>Total Number of Road Accidents and persons killed in Road Accidents on National Highways <br/><br/>S.
